releases.summary: 🔴 0.9.0 IS A MINOR RELEASE BECAUSE IT REMOVES ENVIRONMENT VARIABLES. OPE-2650 sweeps the env-read allowlist down to the maintainer's ruling: env holds the root of trust, what opens the db store, what the platform injects, and per-run test seams. Every other value becomes a setting in Git or an operator secret in the db store. A removed variable that is still set does nothing, so move each value BEFORE you deploy. This entry lists the first set: the access-request wiring and the deprecated `OE_AI_GATEWAY_URL`.
breaking: The access-request flows read no environment variable (OPE-2650). `OE_ACCESS_ADMIN_CHANNEL`, `OE_ACCESS_CONFIG_REPO` and `OE_ACCESS_CONFIG_BASE` are the settings `accessRequests.adminChannel`, `accessRequests.configRepo` and `accessRequests.configBase` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`. `OE_ACCESS_GRANTS_PATH`, `OE_WEBHOOK_HOOKS_PATH`, `OE_AGENTS_PATH` and `OE_CREDENTIAL_BINDINGS_PATH` are gone: each overlay path is a field of the app's `agent/access/access-requests.ts` with a code default (`bindingsPath` is new there). A deployment that sets the variables and does not move the values loses `request_access`, `create_agent`, `declare_webhook`, `propose_mcp_server`, the credential-binding pull request and the directory-group delivery: each one refuses politely as unconfigured. With `github.auth: "token"`, the token also stops reaching the deployment's own repository until `accessRequests.configRepo` is set.

`OE_AI_GATEWAY_URL` is gone (OPE-2650). 0.8.0 deprecated it for `models.targets.gateway.url`. Nothing reads it now, so a deployment that still sets it and has no target `url` sends its model calls to the shipped Vercel AI Gateway endpoint.

`targetBaseUrl` (adapters `model/gateway.ts`) takes no `env` argument, and `DEPRECATED_GATEWAY_URL_ENV` is no longer exported. `gatewayCatalogUrl` (adapters `model/gateway-probe.ts`) takes no argument.

configMigrations.description: If the deployment sets `OE_ACCESS_ADMIN_CHANNEL`, `OE_ACCESS_CONFIG_REPO` or `OE_ACCESS_CONFIG_BASE`, copy each value into `accessRequests: { adminChannel, configRepo, configBase }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`, deploy, then unset the variables (OPE-2650).

If the deployment sets `OE_ACCESS_GRANTS_PATH`, `OE_WEBHOOK_HOOKS_PATH`, `OE_AGENTS_PATH` or `OE_CREDENTIAL_BINDINGS_PATH` to a non-default path, set `grantsPath`, `hooksPath`, `agentsPath` or `bindingsPath` in the object `loadAccessRequests()` returns in `agent/access/access-requests.ts`. A default path needs no step (OPE-2650).

If the deployment still sets `OE_AI_GATEWAY_URL`, move its value to `models: { targets: { gateway: { kind: "vercel-ai-gateway", url: "<the value>" } } }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`, then unset the env var (OPE-2650; the 0.8.0 step of OPE-2556).

manualSteps: BEFORE you deploy 0.9.0, move every removed variable this deployment sets into the line its config migration names, and merge that change in the same deploy. A value left only in the env store is lost at that deploy: the flow it armed turns off with no error. After the deploy, delete the variables from the env store.

releases.summary: 0.8.1 is a patch release. It needs no upgrade step. It has two fixes. The first is on Slack. The second is in core and acts on every surface that marks a message as addressed. First, a person in a 1:1 DM with the Slack bot now sees a 👀 and a `Working...` status line in the DM while the turn runs (OPE-2629). Both signs clear when the turn finishes or waits on the person. A turn that fails does not clear its signs. A group DM shows no signs. The 👀 needs the `reactions:write` scope, and the status line needs the `assistant:write` scope and the agent view. The current Slack manifest grants all three. An install that never re-applied the manifest does not show the matching sign, and logs the fix once per process. Second, the seat no longer skips an addressed ask as a duplicate only because carried history holds an earlier answer to the same words (OPE-2623). On a message that the surface marks as addressed, the seat now needs its own earlier answer to the same ask in the current generation of the window. An answer from before the window last rotated does not count. A message without that mark has no such check. A seat that records no session tail, such as a thread seat or a per-surface seat, has no earlier answer to show, so it cannot skip a marked message as a duplicate. One gap stays: the check can run before the surface records the new message, and then it judges only the earlier messages that wait for an answer. A refused skip writes the new audit row `reply.no_reply_duplicate_refused`.

🔴 0.8.0 IS A MINOR RELEASE BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT AN EXISTING INSTALL DOES. Read the breaking changes and the manual steps BEFORE you deploy. An app on a release older than 0.7.0 must also read every entry between its release and 0.8.0. `oe upgrade` shows them all. These changes alter what an existing install does by default. First, a recurring routine that nobody checks in on now posts a Keep going card after 100 runs, and pauses itself 24 runs later (OPE-2511). A reply in the routine's report thread is a check-in (OPE-2532, OPE-2558). Second, a voice clip that a person sends to the agent is now transcribed and answered on Slack (OPE-2524). Third, workflow discovery: the chief-of-staff watch offers a routine for work or a question that a person repeats on the same weekday, and a shared room gets an offer for work that two or more people there repeat (OPE-2512, OPE-2539, OPE-2550). Fourth, a person's first DM conversation and a room's first conversation may end in one routine offer (OPE-2514). Fifth, a daily retention sweep deletes finished transcripts and conversational state older than 90 days (OPE-2527). Sixth, answers on Slack and Teams change: native thumbs on every answer, numbered source links and up to three suggested follow-ups in a 1:1 conversation, and the Teams AI label on more posts (OPE-2520, OPE-2543, OPE-2516, OPE-2542). Seventh, GitHub sign-in is one declared choice, the App or a personal access token, and `GITHUB_TOKEN` is no longer a silent fallback from the App (OPE-2530). These features are on with no configuration: the "What I do for you" list (OPE-2522); a test run of a routine with every write blocked, on Slack, Teams and Discord (OPE-2515, OPE-2540); Slack agent sessions with native Stop, titles and the "needs you" state (OPE-2519); a watch that a person sets up by asking "tell me when …" (OPE-2510); and Slack canvas and List writes behind an approval card (OPE-2521). Opt-in features: out-of-office cover (OPE-2513, OPE-2534), meetings on Discord voice (OPE-2473), a data policy and provider allowlist on every model call (OPE-2535, OPE-2556), a European model stack (OPE-2531), one-click GitHub App creation (OPE-2529) and the Docker route for a new scaffold (OPE-2405). The new exit kit adds `oe export`, `oe erase` and `oe transcript delete` (OPE-2527, OPE-2560, OPE-2561). No operator-set environment variable is added or removed. `OE_AI_GATEWAY_URL` is deprecated (config migrations). The eve peer stays 0.71.0. The operational store gains five tables (`personal_cover`, `question_ledger`, `room_watch`, `routine_report_thread` and `memory_canvas`). App code can stop compiling: a route key is renamed (`providers` → `providerOrder`), an audit detail type is narrowed, and unreached deep exports are gone. Every install must run `npx oe build --accept`, because core offers eight new roster names. A Slack install must paste the manifest again and reinstall the app, because it gains one bot event and three bot scopes.
breaking: A recurring clock routine that nobody checks in on now pauses itself (OPE-2511). A `cron` or `interval` routine, an only-on-change routine and a durable job count their runs since a person last checked in. After `routines.attentionWarnRuns` runs (shipped 100), the routine posts one Keep going card where its reports land. With no press, it pauses after `routines.attentionPauseRuns` more runs (shipped 24) and posts a Resume card. An hourly routine posts the card about 4 days after the upgrade and pauses about one day later. A press of Keep going, a Resume, `enable_routine`, or a carded edit or rule change is a check-in. One-time and event routines are not counted. To keep the old behaviour, set `routines.attentionWarnRuns: 0` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`.

Voice clips are heard on Slack (OPE-2524). The setting `voiceClips.enabled` ships `true`. An audio file or voice clip that a person sends where the agent already answers (a DM, a group DM, an @mention, or a thread the agent is in) is transcribed through the stack's transcription role and answered as typed text. The audio goes to the transcription role's primary route, and to its fallback route when the primary fails. A clip whose route reports a cost bills to the conversation's spend row. Each message that carries a voice clip writes one `voice.transcribed` audit row, also when no clip is heard, and the row holds no transcript. A clip in a room that did not address the agent is never downloaded. An app that does not pass `TRANSCRIPTION_ROLE` to `registerGatewayMeetingModels` in `agent/agent.ts` (the 0.6.0 template does) hears no clip: the agent gets one line for each clip, which says no speech-to-text model is set up here, so it can tell the person. To turn the feature off, set `voiceClips.enabled: false`.

The chief-of-staff watch offers routines (OPE-2512). Workflow discovery reads the person's own tool-call ledger (`tool_usage`, ids and counts only). When a person ran one connector op on the same UTC weekday in at least `routines.discoveryMinWeeks` (shipped 3) of the last 5 weeks, the watch posts one Set it up / No thanks card in their DM. The latest of those days must be in the last 14 days, and that weekday must hold at least 60% of the op's active days. Each idea is offered once. The watch dial governs it: `none` reads nothing. At most one card goes out per 14 days on `less`, and per 7 days on `more`. Nothing runs until the person presses Set it up. To turn it off, set `routines.discoveryMinWeeks: 0`.

Workflow discovery finds repeated questions and shared-room patterns (OPE-2539). The new hook `hook/question-ledger` records a question that a member asks the agent in their own DM, or with an @mention in a shared room, in a turn that made no connector call. It keeps the question's normalized words for 42 days in the new table `question_ledger`, and never records a person who opted out of the agent remembering their content. A question that a person asks in their own DM on the same UTC weekday in at least `routines.discoveryMinWeeks` of the last 5 weeks gets the same Set it up / No thanks card in that DM, under the same dial and DM-stop holds. A connector op or a question that two or more people repeat in one shared room gets one card in that room, at most one per room per 14 days. A connector op that one person repeats on their own inside the room is left to that person's own discovery, which offers it in their DM when their watch runs. A question that only one person repeats in a room gets no card. A member in the room may answer the card. A room that holds a guest or an outside account gets no card. No thanks is recorded in the new table `room_watch`, and the room is not offered that idea again. `routines.discoveryMinWeeks: 0` turns both off.

A first conversation may end in one routine offer (OPE-2514). For `routines.firstConversationDays` (shipped 3) days after a person's first DM turn creates their watch row, or after the agent first introduces itself in a room, the seat may offer ONE routine that fits what they said they do, in one plain sentence, and hand off the job that creates it. The routine card is the one confirmation. The host ends the offer when the card posts, and a decline or a set-up routine records how it ended. A person whose watch row already exists, and a room already introduced, never get the offer. To turn it off, set `routines.firstConversationDays: 0`.

Slack DM conversations become agent sessions (OPE-2519). A new top-level DM message creates its session with a title made from the words the person typed. The session shows `processing` while a turn runs, and `suspended` ("needs you") when the turn waits on the person. A job that the DM seat forwards to the work session, and that ends waiting on the person (for example an `ask_room` card or a sign-in), also sets `suspended` (OPE-2536). Slack's Stop button cancels the turn by the same road as the ✋ reaction and `/oe stop`. Slack shows the Stop button only after you paste the manifest again (manual steps).

Every person gets the "What I do for you" list (OPE-2522). On Slack it is the first section of the Home tab, with Pause or Remove on a routine in the person's own DM. In a DM, the new tool `doing_for_me` answers "What are you doing for me?" with the same list. It shows only the person's own routines, watch, lent credential grants, DM rules and the cards waiting on them.

A "tell me when …" ask now ends in a watch (OPE-2510). Every live DM and room seat prompt carries a short block. It tells the seat to say the watch back in one sentence and to hand off the job that posts the routine card. The job subscribes to the app's events where the app sends them here, and otherwise sets up an hourly only-on-change check. `create_routine` gains an optional `watchFor`, the condition in plain words. The card headline and the "What I do for you" list read it. Connecting an app still arms nothing. No setting, environment variable, table or roster name is added.

A person can run a routine once as a test (OPE-2515, OPE-2540). The new tool `test_routine` (open tier, like `run_routine_now`) runs the routine's real reads and the real model, blocks every write, and ends with a list of each write it blocked. A workflow tool such as `ask_question` is removed from the test instead, so the list does not name it. It works on Slack (a thread in the routine's own room), on Teams (under a new opening post: a new reply chain in a channel, or a post in a 1:1 chat) and on Discord (in the routine's channel, where the closing summary replies to the test's opening message). An event routine can be tested once it has matched an event: the test replays the last matched event, which the routine row now keeps as `lastEvent` (at most 16,384 characters, without the actor). A finished job, and an event routine that has matched no event yet, cannot be tested. On any other platform `test_routine` refuses with "a test run is not available on this platform". A routine's create and edit replies end with an offer to test it wherever a test can run. Apart from its own test request, a test moves nothing on the routine: not its schedule, its run count or its check-in count. It writes no `routine.fire` audit row. Durable jobs (`create_routine` with `job`) are no longer Slack-only: they also work on Teams and Discord (OPE-2568). Any other platform refuses a durable job in words.

Core offers eight new roster names: `hook/routine-test-run` and `tool/test_routine` (OPE-2515), `schedule/cover-recap` (OPE-2513), `tool/doing_for_me` (OPE-2522), `tool/write_canvas` and `tool/update_list` (OPE-2521), `hook/question-ledger` (OPE-2539) and `hook/routine-report-reply` (OPE-2558). Until `oe build --accept` records them in `roster.lock.json`, the build reports them as unreviewed and `oe build --check` exits 1 (manual steps). With `hook/routine-report-reply` excluded, a native reply in a room with no window does not count as a check-in, and a press still does.

The operational store gains five tables: `personal_cover` (OPE-2513), `question_ledger` and `room_watch` (OPE-2539), `routine_report_thread` (OPE-2532) and `memory_canvas` (OPE-2587). An owner boot creates them on Postgres and on SQLite, with no migration script. Each has row-level security on Postgres. The runtime role gets `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` on `personal_cover`, `room_watch` and `memory_canvas` (no DELETE), `SELECT, INSERT, DELETE` on `question_ledger` (a row older than 42 days is deleted on each append), and `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on `routine_report_thread` (a write deletes the rows past their own expiry). A two-role Postgres deployment runs the owner boot first, then the statements `runtimeRoleGrantsSql` returns (manual steps).

The Slack app manifest gains one bot event, `agent_session_stopped` (OPE-2519), and the `/oe` usage hint gains `cover [on | off]` (OPE-2513) and `suggest [on | off]` (OPE-2550). The event needs `chat:write`, which the manifest already requests. The manifest also gains three bot scopes: `lists:read` and `lists:write`, for the agent's List changes (OPE-2521), and `canvases:read`, which finds a memory canvas made before 0.8.0 (OPE-2587). A scope change needs a reinstall of the app.

The agent writes Slack canvases and Lists (OPE-2521). Two new worker tools, `write_canvas` and `update_list`, change only a canvas or a List that the asking room shows, or create a canvas in that room. Each write posts a `canvas.write` or `list.write` card (`gate:member`). A List card quotes every row, and a canvas card quotes the start of the text and says how much it does not show. Nothing changes until a person approves or the room's approver chain lowers the card. `write_canvas` refuses the channel's domain memory canvas, at propose time and at approval, and it refuses when its lookup cannot confirm that the target is not the memory canvas (OPE-2585). On a free Slack workspace whose channel already has a canvas tab, an approved create fails with one line that says the plan allows one canvas tab per channel (OPE-2582). Each approved write writes one `canvas.write` or `list.write` audit row, which holds no text. A Slack app without `lists:read` and `lists:write` fails every List change with `missing_scope`: a row change before its card, an added row after the approval (manual steps).

`GITHUB_TOKEN` is no longer a fallback from the GitHub App (OPE-2530). The new setting `github.auth` ships `"app"`: every GitHub call then mints through the App, and a repository the App is not installed on is refused by name instead of using the token. A deployment that has NO GitHub App and relied on `GITHUB_TOKEN` for pull requests, PR reads or ticket actions must set `github: { auth: "token" }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`, or those calls refuse. In token mode the token reaches only this deployment's own repository (`OE_ACCESS_CONFIG_REPO`) and the repositories `github.tokenRepos` names, `checkout_repo` now works there through the sandbox firewall, and the GitHub conversation surface is off. See docs/capabilities/source-control.md.

A member's reply in a routine's report thread is now a check-in (OPE-2532). It starts the routine's Keep going count again, as a press does. It counts only a person whom the host's trust gate rated `principal` or `peer` on that wake: never a bot, an author with no id, or an author in a room the gate did not confirm as internal. In an internal room the gate rates by refutation: a Slack guest or outside account does not count, but a Slack member lookup that cannot answer leaves the room's verdict in place, and on Discord and Notion only the operator's author-trust register refutes a person. The reply must land in the report's own thread within 30 days, and the agent must hear it: in a room that hears only @mentions, only a reply that mentions the agent counts. A reply never resumes a paused routine. Each report post writes ids only to the new table `routine_report_thread`, and each counted reply writes a `routine.checkin` audit row with `detail.via: "reply"`. No setting turns the reply leg off on its own; `routines.attentionWarnRuns: 0` turns the whole check-in off.

A reply to a NATIVE fire's report, and a reply on Teams, Linear and Discord, is now a check-in too (OPE-2558). A fire with `delegation.oneshotAgent` off, or in a room with no seat, posts its report through the per-surface reply door, and that door now records the report's thread on Slack, Teams and Linear. On a room with no window, the new hook `hook/routine-report-reply` counts a member's message in that thread. On Linear's native road only a reply nested under the report comment counts. On Teams a reply in the reply chain under a channel report counts. On Linear a reply nested under a top-level report comment counts. On Discord a thread opened off the report counts. A test run records nothing. Each counted reply writes the same `routine.checkin` row with `detail.via: "reply"`. No table, setting or environment variable is added.

The native Slack @mention door now stamps a guest as a non-member (OPE-2572). It runs the same `users.info` probe and the same `oe_chat_nonmember` stamp as the other Slack roads. A guest's native @mention or DM then seeds the turn's taint, is refused on the member plane, and is not a report-thread check-in. The room leg runs on that door too: in a channel the operator declared `public`, every native @mention is stamped, a member's included, and so is one in an undeclared channel when `taint.undeclaredSurface` is `"mark"`. The probe fails open: when `users.info` cannot answer, nothing is stamped. On the shipped `externalPolicy` grains the front route already withholds or silences a guest's mention, so that change shows only on the `taint` / `engage` opt-out pair. The front route silences a mention in a declared-`public` channel only under `roomGrain: "silent"`, so a member's mention there is stamped wherever `roomGrain` is `engage`. A member's mention in an undeclared channel under `taint.undeclaredSurface: "mark"` is stamped on every grain, except in a Slack Connect channel under `roomGrain: "silent"`, which the front route silences.

The domain memory canvas now rewrites and takes down only its own canvas (OPE-2587). Slack shows a channel's canvases as tabs, and a canvas the agent creates for a person through `write_canvas` has the app's bot user as its creator too. The app now records the id of each memory canvas it creates, and it does not rewrite, clear or refuse to append to any other canvas. `write_canvas` now refuses a title or text that quotes the memory canvas footer line, so the agent never writes that line into a canvas it makes for a person. A person who types the line by hand into a canvas the agent made, in a channel that does not show its recorded memory canvas, makes the next memory write take that canvas as the memory canvas. A memory canvas made before 0.8.0 is found as before when Slack names it in the channel's canvas field. When Slack shows it only as a tab, it is found by a line its footer carries, and that read needs the new `canvases:read` bot scope (re-apply the Slack manifest). Until then a channel that does not show its recorded memory canvas and shows any canvas tab the app made (a memory canvas or a `write_canvas` canvas) cannot be judged: its refresh records `failed` and creates no new memory canvas, its take-down records `clear-failed` even when no memory is on screen, and nothing is overwritten.

A daily retention sweep now deletes old data (OPE-2527). Each night it deletes finished session transcripts on the local workflow world, and conversational state in the operational store, once they are older than 90 days: conversation tails and DM summaries, job results, Slack file links, captured webhook bodies, status lines and the words of repeated questions. The audit log, the usage ledgers, memory and config are never aged out. To keep the old behaviour, set `retention.sessionTranscriptDays: 0` and `retention.storedStateDays: 0` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`. Run `oe export --out DIR` before you deploy if you want a copy of what the first sweep removes. On Vercel the export reads each session transcript through the deployment, so set `OE_DEPLOY_CONTROL_TOKEN` and the deployment URL (`OE_DEPLOY_BASE_URL`, `OE_DEPLOY_ALIAS` or `E2E_TARGET_URL`) in the shell first. Without them the export names each transcript as unreached and copies none.

A domain or role model route's key `providers` is renamed `providerOrder` (OPE-2556). The gateway always read it as an order hint, never as an allowlist, and the old name hid that. A route that still names `providers` fails typecheck. It also fails config load, with an error that names the new key, in an app whose `agent/lib/register-config.ts` calls `assertRouteTargets`, as the 0.8.0 template does. Without that line and without a typecheck, the old key is ignored and the order hint is lost (config migrations).

Answers on Slack and Teams change, with no setting (OPE-2520, OPE-2543, OPE-2516, OPE-2542). Every finished model answer, in any room, shows the platform's native thumbs up and down (Slack `feedback_buttons`, Teams `feedbackLoopEnabled`). A press writes a new `reply.feedback` audit row, and a Teams thumbs-down comment records only its length. In a 1:1 conversation only (a Slack DM, the side panel included, or a Teams personal chat), an answer fed by a first-party read shows up to 5 numbered source links, GitHub issues and pull requests and Notion pages included, and it may carry up to 3 suggested follow-ups of at most 75 characters each. A shared room gets no source link and no follow-up. On Slack a press of a follow-up wakes the DM seat as a typed message, with every gate applied, and each answer takes one press. On Slack an answer now posts as `section` blocks, and it posts again as text alone if Slack refuses the blocks. On Teams every post of model text carries the AI generated label, proactive DMs and the domain-answer fallback included. Host text (cards, notices) stays unlabelled. No scope, manifest or roster change is needed.

Approval text is shorter, and an action posts one message (OPE-2490, OPE-2489). `/oe budget raise|clear` posts no receipt when its card posted in the asker's room. The decision notice no longer repeats the card: when someone else decided, or the request expired, the asker gets one short line. A Slack card redraws in place on a sweep or a session-grant release. A click refusal is one plain notice, ephemeral on Slack (before, a public thread post). A failed act reads "⚠️ Approved by …, but it failed", and the raw error goes to the audit row only. A failed durable decline reads "I could not save the decline", and the cause goes to an `approval.failed` row with `phase: "decline"` (OPE-2549). The spend card's visible line names the figures ("From $50/mo to $2,575/mo"), and its pricing caveat moves to the message metadata.

Every seat prompt gains a "Your admins and your setup" block, read from config and env (OPE-2492). The agent can now say who its admins are and whether the asker is one. The `agent_version` tool gains a `setup` field: the admins, the connected apps and each setup gap with the one step that fixes it. It shows the repository and the settings only to an admin. The host now renders a Slack or Markdown link whose target is a relative path as its label only.

Slack `/oe` commands read trust more strictly and more exactly (OPE-2579, OPE-2588). In a Slack 1:1 DM, each `/oe` command now asks `users.info` who the invoker is (at most 1.5 s). A guest or Slack Connect account reads `external` even under a workspace vouch, so a guest's `/oe watch more|less` is refused. Every watch refusal, from the command or the Home tab, writes a new `personal_watch.dial.refused` audit row. A channel `/oe` command now reads the room's real trust and stamps it only when `users.info` confirms the invoker as a member. So a member in an internal, unshared channel can now run room commands such as `/oe suggest on|off`, where before every channel `/oe` read as `external`. In an internal Slack channel, `/oe budget` and `/oe budget status` refuse a guest, or anyone `users.info` cannot confirm, in one line. In an internal channel, `/oe budget raise` and `/oe budget clear` now read the internal domain's caps for every invoker, guests included, and a member's `/oe budget` does too. Before, they read the external domain's caps. Discord and Teams do not change.

Revoking a person's link set now ends what they lend (OPE-2504). A manual `revoke_link_set` and the automatic Slack offboarding also revoke every credential grant the person lends and forget their personal browser profile. Before, both survived. This runs only for confirmed accounts, never for a `suggested` one. A failure is named in `holdingFailures` on the audit row.

A delegated worker now reads the room and the thread that its job came from, with `read_work_channel` and `read_work_thread`, on the seat's own access and with no work grant (OPE-2491). This covers Slack, Discord, Teams, Notion, Linear and GitHub, not email. A read of any other room still needs a work grant.

The new exit kit commands work as follows (OPE-2527, OPE-2560, OPE-2565, OPE-2561, OPE-2574). `oe erase` first ends the person's authority: it revokes their link set or purges its credentials, revokes the grants they lend and forgets their personal browser. It then deletes rows. When a saved browser profile is in reach, pass `--box-backend vercel|docker`; without it the command changes nothing, exits 1 and names the accounts. A failed provider token revocation is retried once, then reported. `oe erase` exits 1 on any authority or revocation failure, and its `exit.person_erased` row counts each part. `oe erase` names each session transcript it could not delete: nothing can delete a transcript on Vercel's hosted store. On that store, `oe transcript delete` says the session is NOT deleted and exits 1. On Postgres, `oe export` reads in pages of at most 8 MiB, and reads a wider row alone, so a large store exports under Neon's 64 MiB response cap. A single row wider than that cap cannot come back through Neon's HTTP driver. On a host with no workflow directory, such as Vercel, it reads each transcript through the deployment (see the retention entry).

Audit rows change (OPE-2545, OPE-2549, OPE-1940, OPE-2591, OPE-2600, OPE-2603). Every audit writer, provider bundles included, scrubs error text and caps it at 300 characters. Audit writers that hold a binding stamp the resolved `surfaceMode`, so `query_analytics` shows fewer `(unclassified)` rows. Older rows stay as they are. A delegated worker's `reply.post` and `reply.edit` rows carry the seat wake's id in `wakeId`. A failed `memory.canvas_refresh` row carries `slackError`, `slackMethod` and `slackNeeded` (for example `canvases:read`). A seat's `work` forward that fails to deliver writes a new `work.forward_failed` row. 🔴 App or bundle code that writes audit rows: `appendAudit`'s `detail` and `auditToolAction`'s `detail` are now typed `AuditDetail`. A plain string under an error-named key (`err`, `error…`, `…Error…`) no longer compiles. Wrap it with `auditErrorDetail(e).error` or `scrubAuditText(…)`, both exported from `@open-everywhere/core/agent/adapter-api.js`.

Value exports that no package read are no longer exported, and some are deleted (OPE-2142, OPE-2143, OPE-2507). Each module under a package's `agent/` tree is a published subpath, so app code that deep-imports one of these names no longer compiles. Examples: `appStaticToken`, `appConnectToken` and `userInteractiveOAuth` (core `agent/connections/connector-auth.js`), `subjectLabel` and `configureLocalWsProxy` (adapters), and `slackDmWake`, `slackWorkspaceVouched` and `liveTeamsFrontPlan` (providers). `adapter-api.js`, `index.js` and `contributions.js` do not change. Import from `@open-everywhere/core/agent/adapter-api.js` where it holds the name.

Fixes that change what a person sees, with no setting. A Slack edit that changes no text, quote or file no longer wakes the seat, and Slack's @mention event pair no longer refuses the answer as stale (OPE-2576, OPE-2577). A work session starts each forwarded job once, and its turn ends when every job has started or gone back to the seat (OPE-2613). A Teams DM work session no longer fails on a long hook token (OPE-2614). When a `work` forward fails, the seat gives back what it owed only when the job never started, and it names no cause (OPE-2603). A plain follow-up in a Teams reply chain that the agent was @mentioned into now reaches the seat as an engaged follow-up (OPE-2610). Home tab Remove on a DM rule ("Approve, and allow things like this") now works (OPE-2496). The seat answers a fact the conversation already holds, with no memory lookup first (OPE-2601). The agent posts in a granted arrival channel (OPE-2595). The webhook tools name apps such as GitHub whose own events reach the deployment, so the agent sets up an event watch on them (OPE-2609). The chat read tools list each message's files by id, name and media type, with no URL (OPE-2489).

On Vercel, the `otlp` telemetry destination exports spans to Vercel's own OTel collector again, so a Vercel OpenTelemetry integration receives spans with no app change (OPE-2358). It reads the platform-injected `VERCEL_OTEL_ENDPOINTS`, `VERCEL_OTEL_ENDPOINTS_PORT` and `VERCEL_OTEL_ENDPOINTS_PROTOCOL`, which no operator sets. The spans keep the metadata-only trace policy. Open Everywhere's own telemetry heartbeat now reports Slack as a surface also when the bot token was stored through `/setup` (OPE-2241).

The email `event_dedupe` sweep keeps a delivery claim for 72 h, not 24 h, so a webhook that AgentMail retries more than 24 h later no longer wakes the seat twice (OPE-2573). A provider bundle's `markEventSeen` TTL must stay under `EVENT_DEDUPE_MAX_RETENTION_MS`, now 72 h and exported from `@open-everywhere/core/agent/adapter-api.js`.

`oe upgrade --plan` prints each release's new defaults as `DEFAULT` lines, and `oe upgrade` repeats them at the end (OPE-2517). An installed 0.7.0 `oe` prints no `DEFAULT` line for 0.8.0. To see them before the install, run `npx -p @open-everywhere/core@0.8.0 oe upgrade --plan --to 0.8.0`.

The template's seat prompt changes (OPE-2601, OPE-2607). The template's `agent/instructions.md` § Memory gains the paragraph that starts "A fact this conversation already holds is not a lookup." `oe upgrade` never copies `agent/instructions.md`. Without the paragraph, the base lookup-first rule outvotes the core fix, and the seat posts a deferral before it answers a held fact (manual steps).

configMigrations.description: A deployment with no GitHub App that used `GITHUB_TOKEN` (OPE-2530): add `github: { auth: "token", tokenRepos: ["owner/repo", …] }` to `SETTINGS_OVERRIDES` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`. List in `tokenRepos` each repository besides `OE_ACCESS_CONFIG_REPO` that the agent works on. A deployment that has the App needs no settings change. Install the App on every repository that the token reached through the fallback, or calls on those repositories refuse.

Rename `providers` to `providerOrder` on every domain and role model route (`models: { primary | utility | supervisor: { … } }`) (OPE-2556). The value does not change. For a provider ALLOWLIST, which `providers` never was, set `models.targets.gateway.providers.only` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`.

If the deployment sets `OE_AI_GATEWAY_URL`, move its value to `models: { targets: { gateway: { kind: "vercel-ai-gateway", url: "<the value>" } } }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`, then unset the env var (OPE-2556). The env var still works in 0.8.0 for the `gateway` target, and the process warns once, the first time the process reads the target. It goes away in the next release. When both are set, the setting wins.

manualSteps: Run `npx oe build --accept`, then commit `roster.lock.json`. One run records the eight new core names: `hook/question-ledger`, `hook/routine-report-reply`, `hook/routine-test-run`, `schedule/cover-recap`, `tool/doing_for_me`, `tool/test_routine`, `tool/update_list` and `tool/write_canvas`. Without this step `oe build --check` exits 1.

On a two-role Postgres deployment (a separate non-owner runtime role), run ONE boot as the owner role BEFORE the runtime tier reaches 0.8.0. That boot creates `personal_cover`, `question_ledger`, `room_watch`, `routine_report_thread` and `memory_canvas`. Then run the statements `runtimeRoleGrantsSql("<runtime role>")` returns, as the owner (`docs/extending/database.md`, step 3). Without the grants the runtime role gets `permission denied` on these tables: `/oe cover` and the `cover-recap` schedule fail; the question ledger records nothing and room discovery offers nothing; a reply in a report thread does not count as a check-in (a press still does); and a channel with no memory canvas yet gets none (its refresh records `failed`). A single-role deployment (the owner role runs the app) needs no step.

The owner boot also creates two indexes for room discovery's per-room reads: `tool_usage_org_surface_ts` on `tool_usage` and `question_ledger_org_surface_ts` on `question_ledger` (OPE-2550). On Postgres, a plain index build blocks writes to its table while it runs. On a large `tool_usage` table, create the index first, as the owner, with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS tool_usage_org_surface_ts ON tool_usage (org_id, surface_key, ts)`. The boot then finds it and builds nothing.

Re-apply the Slack app manifest on every EXISTING Slack app. Run `surface_manifest` (or open `/setup`) and paste the manifest it returns, or make the changes by hand: add the bot event `agent_session_stopped` under Event Subscriptions, add `cover [on | off]` and `suggest [on | off]` to the `/oe` usage hint, and add the bot scopes `lists:read`, `lists:write` and `canvases:read`. Then reinstall the app to the workspace (OAuth & Permissions, Reinstall to Workspace), because the scopes changed. Slack shows its Stop button on an agent session only to an app subscribed to that event (OPE-2519). Without the two Lists scopes, every List change fails with `missing_scope`: a row change before its card, an added row after the approval (OPE-2521). Without `canvases:read`, a channel that does not show its recorded memory canvas and shows any canvas tab the app made cannot be judged: its refresh records `failed` and creates no new memory canvas, its take-down records `clear-failed` even when no memory is on screen, and `write_canvas` refuses a change to another canvas the agent made there (OPE-2587). Everything else works without this step.

Account for the new schedule that every 0.8.0 install mounts: `cover-recap`, every 5 minutes (`*/5 * * * *`). It sends nothing until a person turns cover on. Update a cron budget or an allowlist that lists schedules by name.

Check each recurring routine that runs with nobody watching, for example an hourly report to an empty channel. Each one posts a Keep going card about 100 runs after the upgrade, and pauses 24 runs later with no press. Press Keep going on the card, or raise `routines.attentionWarnRuns` (`0` turns the check off).

Decide whether voice clips may leave the deployment. A heard clip goes to the transcription role's routes in `agent/model/stacks.ts`. If your data policy refuses that, set `voiceClips.enabled: false` in `agent/settings/settings.ts` before you deploy.

Optional — out-of-office cover (OPE-2513). Nothing to configure. A member turns it on in their own DM with `/oe cover on [until YYYY-MM-DD]`. While cover is on, the agent answers questions that name the person in its channels, with a `Cover for <name>, who is away:` label. `/oe cover off`, or the end date, sends one recap to the person's DM. It works in Slack channels, in Teams channels on the single-window path and in vouched Discord guild channels (OPE-2534). On Discord, `/oe` gains a `cover` group (`on`, `off`, `status`). The deployment re-registers `/oe` in its declared guilds on its next cold start. A guild command does not reach a DM, and `on` runs in a DM. So run `npm run register:discord-commands` once with `DISCORD_GUILD_ID` unset to register `/oe` globally. A global command takes up to an hour to appear. A Discord DM binds `external` unless your trust declaration makes it `internal`, so `on` refuses there until it does. A Teams recap shows a question from a standard channel only. The Teams roster read is not yet proven on a live tenant. A Discord recap shows a question only from a channel the person can view.

Optional — create a GitHub App in one click (OPE-2529). The ops MCP server's new tool `surface_app_create` (`{ "surface": "github", "baseUrl": "https://<your-deploy-url>" }`) generates the App manifest, and writes the App's id, private key and webhook secret into `.env.local`. It refuses to overwrite names that `.env.local` already holds. An existing App needs no change. See `docs/deploy/surfaces/github.md`.

Optional — turn eve's CLI telemetry off in an app scaffolded before 0.8.0 (OPE-2526). `oe upgrade` does not rewrite `package.json` or `Dockerfile`. Put `EVE_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 ` in front of `eve` in the `dev`, `build` and `start` scripts. If the app has its own `Dockerfile`, add `ENV EVE_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` to its build stage and to its runtime stage. The template had no `Dockerfile` before 0.8.0, and the 0.8.0 template `Dockerfile` already sets it. On Vercel the `build` script carries it, so no project environment variable is needed. The prefix is POSIX shell syntax: on Windows, use WSL or set npm's `script-shell` to a POSIX shell. Without this step eve sends one event for each `eve` command, and the app works the same.

Optional — demand a data policy of every model call (OPE-2535). Add `models: { dataPolicy: { zeroRetention: true, noTraining: true, region: "eu" } }` (any subset) to `agent/settings/settings.ts`. The model adapter puts the rows on every model call, side calls included, and a call that no provider can serve fails closed with an error that names the rows. Check your stack first: `region: "eu"` refuses every model of the `chinese-open-weights` stack today. With any row set, the `deepinfra` transcription route refuses. With no row set, no request changes. Side calls (the judges, the meeting recap, the image describer) and a declared subagent's model now reach the gateway through the same provider as the turn, so `OE_AI_GATEWAY_URL` and the self-host egress proxy's host plane now cover them too. See `docs/extending/models-and-gateway.md`.

Optional — name where model calls go, and which providers may serve them (OPE-2556). `models.targets.gateway` takes `url`, `providers: { only?, order? }` and `options`. `providers.only` is a demand on every model call, side calls included: a model with no allowed provider fails closed with an error that names the row. A route or a stack role can pick another named target with `via`. Before you deploy a change to `models.targets`, `models.dataPolicy` or the stack, run `npm run check:model-config`: it reads the gateway's public endpoints for the stack roles, the gateway transcription routes, the domain routes and `models.force`, and names a demand no provider can meet. On a deployment, the `model-route` row of `/eve/v1/oe/status` turns `no` on the same check, without the names, but only when `agent/agent.ts` calls `registerModelConfigCheck` (from `@open-everywhere/adapters/agent/model/gateway-probe.js`), as the 0.8.0 template does. Without that call the row does not check the model config. See `docs/extending/models-and-gateway.md`.

Optional — add the model config check to an app scaffolded before 0.8.0 (OPE-2563). The template now ships `scripts/model-config-check.ts` and the script line `"check:model-config": "node --import tsx scripts/model-config-check.ts"`, and the setup skill runs `npm run check:model-config` after the model settings are written. `oe upgrade` adds no script line to `package.json` and copies no file under `scripts/`. Copy the file from the 0.8.0 `@open-everywhere/create` template, add the line to `scripts` in `package.json`, and sync `.claude/skills/quickstart-open-everywhere/SKILL.md` and `AGENTS.md` from the same template. `npx oe upgrade --plan` lists each scaffolded file that differs.

To send a bare model id through your stack's targets (OPE-2566), add the line `registerBareModelRoutes(Object.values(MODELS));` after the `MODELS` object in `agent/model/models.ts`, with `import { registerBareModelRoutes } from "@open-everywhere/core/agent/model/bare-model-via.js";`, as the 0.8.0 template does. A bare model id is a declared subagent's `model` or the model of eve's `evaluate()`. With the line, a bare id goes through the target of the stack role that names it, else the primary role's target. Without it, every bare id still goes through the `gateway` target, and `npm run check:model-config` says so. An app whose roles all use the `gateway` target sees no change.

Optional — the `chinese-open-weights` stack's four text roles moved from `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash-0731` to `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash` in the template (OPE-2531). Your app's `agent/model/stacks.ts` keeps its own model. To follow, change those four ids there and add `"deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash": { inPerMtok: 0.3, outPerMtok: 1.2 }` to `agent/spend/model-pricing.ts`, or `npm run lint:model-ids` fails. The measured rate is about 2x the input and 4x the output price of the old pin.

Optional — a third stack, `european-open-weights` (OPE-2531): Mistral Small 4 (`mistral/mistral-small`) in every role, vision included, each role `via: "mistral"`. To add it, copy its entries in `STACKS` and `TRANSCRIPTION` from the template's `agent/model/stacks.ts`, add the `mistral` target to `models.targets` in `agent/settings/settings.ts` (`mistral: { kind: "vercel-ai-gateway", providers: { only: ["mistral"] }, dataPolicy: { zeroRetention: true } }`, beside your `gateway` target), and add `"mistral/mistral-small": { inPerMtok: 0.15, outPerMtok: 0.6 }` to `agent/spend/model-pricing.ts`. For the side calls to use the same target, also copy the template's `via: MODELS.<role>.via` on each `registerGateway…` call and on `gatewayModelResolver` in `agent/agent.ts`, and `SUPERVISOR_VIA` in `agent/memory/config/domains/org.ts`. Without them those calls go through the `gateway` target. A target now takes `dataPolicy`: rows that every call through it demands on top of `models.dataPolicy`. Its transcription routes are your own servers: Voxtral at `http://voxtral:8000/v1`, then Qwen3-ASR at `http://qwen3-asr:8000/v1`.

Optional — read where your data lives (OPE-2528). Run `npx oe sovereignty --host vercel` (or `--host docker`) in the app: for each piece of data it prints where it lives, which region and which company could be compelled to hand it over, from your own settings, roster and `.env.local`. It changes nothing. Restart the ops MCP server to get its new read-only `sovereignty` tool, which returns the same map. See `docs/security/sovereignty.md`.

If `oe upgrade` from 0.7.0 or earlier stops at `npm run build` with "The Docker sandbox provider requires a running Docker daemon", run `npx oe upgrade` again, or start the daemon first. The retry runs the 0.8.0 `oe` the install put in place, and it resumes. On a host where `docker version` does not answer, and when the app's `build` script ends in `eve build`, its build step builds a failed build again with `--skip-sandbox-prewarm` and says so in one line (OPE-2353). eve says that output may not be deployable, so do not start or deploy it. A Vercel deploy builds again on Vercel.

Merge the template's new seat-prompt paragraph (OPE-2607). Copy the paragraph that starts "**A fact this conversation already holds is not a lookup.**" from the 0.8.0 template's `agent/instructions.md` § Memory into the app's `agent/instructions.md`. `oe upgrade --plan` lists the file as different.
Sync `.claude/skills/upgrade-open-everywhere/SKILL.md` from the 0.8.0 template (OPE-2517). The skill now stops on each new default before the deploy.

Optional — meetings on Discord voice (OPE-2473). Add a `platform: "discord"` rule to `agent/meetings/policy.ts` that lists the allowed server ids in `guilds`; config load refuses an empty list. Redeploy the `deploy/discord-relay` image, which asks for the non-privileged Guild Voice States intent and forwards the voice credentials, and the `deploy/meeting-bot` image. The bot needs View Channel, Connect and Send Messages in the voice channel. It posts a recording notice first and does not record when it cannot. An older relay cannot start a Discord meeting. See `docs/capabilities/meetings.md`.

Optional — the Docker route (OPE-2405). The 0.8.0 template adds `Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `docker-compose.yml` and `deploy/egress-proxy/`. `oe upgrade` copies none of them, and `oe upgrade --plan` lists them as missing. To run the app on your own server, copy them from the template. The template's `agent/settings/settings.ts` also declares `sandbox: { selfHostBackend: "justbash" }`, which is development-grade isolation; core's shipped default stays `docker`. A Vercel app can ignore them, or list them in `.oe-template-ignore`.

Self-host from a clone of this repository only: the egress proxy's Squid helper is renamed `deploy/egress-proxy/control/helper.cjs` (it was `helper.js`, OPE-2619). If you keep your own `squid.conf`, change its `external_acl_type` line to `/usr/bin/node /opt/oe-egress/control/helper.cjs`, then rebuild the proxy. Without the change Squid cannot start the helper, so the proxy fails or refuses every request. A scaffolded app is not affected: its Docker route is new in 0.8.0 (OPE-2405).
newDefaults: An unwatched recurring routine posts a Keep going card after 100 runs and pauses 24 runs later (OPE-2511). To turn it off, set `routines.attentionWarnRuns: 0` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`.

A member's reply in a routine's report thread counts as a check-in (OPE-2532). No setting turns off this leg alone. To turn off the whole check-in, set `routines.attentionWarnRuns: 0` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`.
A voice clip sent to the agent on Slack is transcribed and answered (OPE-2524). To turn it off, set `voiceClips.enabled: false` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`.

The chief-of-staff watch offers a routine for work that a person repeats on the same weekday (OPE-2512). To turn it off, set `routines.discoveryMinWeeks: 0` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`. A person whose watch dial is `none` gets no offer.

Workflow discovery also offers a routine for a question that a person asks the agent in their own DM again and again on the same weekday, and asks a shared room about work that two or more people there repeat (OPE-2539). To turn both off, with the person's discovery, set `routines.discoveryMinWeeks: 0` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`. To stop the question ledger alone, exclude `hook/question-ledger` under `core.exclude` in `roster.config.ts`, with a reason, before `npx oe build --accept`. A person in a shared room stops that room's suggestions with `/oe suggest off`, and a member lifts the stop with `/oe suggest on` (OPE-2550). Room discovery reads each room's ledgers on their own, with no cap for the whole organisation, and every stop, gap or refused card it holds a room back for files one `room_watch.silence` row.

Every person gets the "What I do for you" list on the Slack Home tab and the `doing_for_me` tool in a DM (OPE-2522). No setting turns off the Home tab list. To remove the tool, exclude `tool/doing_for_me` under `core.exclude` in `roster.config.ts`, with a reason, before `npx oe build --accept`.

On Slack, Teams and Discord, a person can run a routine once as a test with every write blocked, through the `test_routine` tool (OPE-2515, OPE-2540). An event routine can be tested once it has matched an event. No setting in `agent/settings/settings.ts` turns it off. To remove it, exclude `tool/test_routine` under `core.exclude` in `roster.config.ts`, with a reason, before `npx oe build --accept`. Keep `hook/routine-test-run` mounted while the tool is mounted. The hook marks a test's session, and the write fence blocks writes only in a marked session. With the hook excluded, `test_routine` queues no test, the create and edit replies offer none, and the dispatcher refuses a test that was already requested and tells the room why (OPE-2546). With only the tool excluded, the create and edit replies still offer a test.
A person's first DM conversation, and a room's first conversation, may end in one routine offer (OPE-2514). To turn it off, set `routines.firstConversationDays: 0` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`.

GitHub calls go through the GitHub App only, and `GITHUB_TOKEN` is no longer a fallback (OPE-2530). The new setting `github.auth` ships `"app"`. To keep using `GITHUB_TOKEN`, set `github: { auth: "token", tokenRepos: ["owner/repo", …] }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`, and list in `tokenRepos` each repository besides `OE_ACCESS_CONFIG_REPO` that the agent works on (see the config migration).

A Slack DM conversation becomes an agent session, with a title and the "needs you" state (OPE-2519). Slack's Stop button appears only after you paste the manifest again (manual steps). No setting turns it off.

An app is offered as an event watch only when its events reach this deployment (OPE-2547). GitHub needs `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, Linear a webhook signing secret, and Notion an inbound secret. Any other app takes the polling road. `create_routine` refuses an event routine on an app whose events do not reach here. The dispatcher posts one line into the room of an armed event routine whose app stops delivering, and one more when it delivers again. From the first tick after the deploy, each event routine on such an app posts that line once, at most 10 per tick. No setting turns it off. A bundle that registers an event normalizer of its own must also call `registerEventReach`, or its source is never offered as an event watch.

The agent can create and change Slack canvases and add or change rows in Slack Lists, behind an approval card (OPE-2521). No setting turns it off. To remove a tool, exclude `tool/write_canvas` or `tool/update_list` under `core.exclude` in `roster.config.ts`, with a reason, before `npx oe build --accept`.

A NEW scaffold turns eve's own CLI telemetry off (OPE-2526). eve 0.71.0 posts the command name, the eve version, the platform, a random installation id and a salted hash of the git remote URL or of the working directory to `telemetry.vercel.com` on each `eve` command. A new scaffold's `dev`, `build` and `start` scripts and both stages of its `Dockerfile` set `EVE_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1`. An app scaffolded before 0.8.0 keeps eve's telemetry on until you take the manual step above. The script prefix is POSIX shell syntax. On Windows, use WSL or set npm's `script-shell` to a POSIX shell. Open Everywhere's own telemetry is unchanged, and `OE_TELEMETRY` still switches it.

The org retention setting ages out finished transcripts and conversational state after 90 days (OPE-2527). To turn it off, set `retention.sessionTranscriptDays: 0` and `retention.storedStateDays: 0` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`.
Every finished answer on Slack and Teams shows native thumbs up and down, and a press writes a `reply.feedback` audit row (OPE-2520). No setting turns it off.
In a 1:1 conversation on Slack or Teams, an answer may show up to 5 numbered source links and up to 3 suggested follow-ups (OPE-2520, OPE-2543, OPE-2516). No setting turns them off.
Revoking a person's link set, by hand or by Slack offboarding, also revokes the credential grants they lend and forgets their personal browser (OPE-2504). No setting turns it off.

releases.summary: 🔴 0.7.0 IS A MINOR RELEASE BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT PEOPLE SEE AND WHAT AN EXISTING INSTALL DOES. Read the breaking changes and the manual steps BEFORE you deploy. An app on a release older than 0.6.0 must also read every entry between its release and 0.7.0. `oe upgrade` shows them all. Five changes alter what an existing install does by default. First, person-facing text is shorter and plainer (OPE-2480, OPE-2486, OPE-2481, OPE-2487). An approval card is now a headline, one consequence line and the buttons. A decided card is one line. A failed turn no longer shows the raw error in the room. Seats no longer narrate a hand-off or repeat what a card shows. Second, replies no longer carry the "Sources read this turn" footer (OPE-2487). The sources go to the `reply.provenance` audit row instead. Third, one outbound guard rewrites raw ids into names on every surface (OPE-2482). A new seat tool, `look_up`, resolves a name. Fourth, each member's DM turn enrols them in the chief-of-staff watch at `less` (OPE-2422). The watch reads nothing until you declare a personal source. Fifth, Teams changes in five ways (OPE-2455, OPE-2446, OPE-2443, OPE-2444, OPE-2445, OPE-2447). The bot refuses a non-Teams client with 403. A 1:1 chat with a home-tenant member is now verified. `/oe` commands work. The agent posts an intro once in each channel. A chat approval card posts in that chat. These features stay off until you declare them: Google Chat as a surface (the new package `@open-everywhere/provider-google-chat`, OPE-2442); inbound A2A calls from another organisation's agent (`a2a.inbound`, OPE-2448); Okta Cross App Access sign-in for personal connections (OPE-2453); teach a task by demonstration in the person's own browser (OPE-2454); and a person's request to another bot in chat (OPE-2426). You can now turn on meeting recaps: OPE-2461 and OPE-2464 landed, so the meeting policy accepts `enabled: true`. No environment variable is added or removed. The eve peer stays 0.71.0. The operational store gains two tables (`personal_watch`, `meeting_data`). Every install must run `npx oe build --accept`, because core offers five new roster names.
breaking: Approval cards are compact on Slack, Teams and Discord (OPE-2481). A pending card shows a headline, at most one consequence line, a taint line when it applies, then "Asked by … · expires …" and the buttons. The "Approval requested: <kind>" line and the detail block are gone. A decided card is one line: "✅ Approved by …", "❌ Rejected by …" or "⏰ Expired". On Slack the kind and the card id move to the message metadata (`event_type: "oe_approval_card"`) and to the first block id (`oe_approval_card:<kind>:<id>`). This needs no new scope. App code that imports `approvalLabel` from `@open-everywhere/core/agent/adapter-api.js` no longer compiles: the export is removed. Use `pendingCardLines`, `cardFooter` and `decidedCardLine` instead.

Core rewords person-facing text (OPE-2486, OPE-2480). A failed turn now says "Sorry, something went wrong…". The raw error goes to the logs only, never to the room. A failed `/oe` command shows its person-facing text or a generic line. `/oe status` renames five labels: `deployment sha` is now `build`, `primary model` is `main model`, `utility model` is `helper model`, `memory provider` is `memory`, and `compaction fires at` is `summarised at`. Core also rewords the budget, routine, connector, onboarding and status messages. A routine notice no longer shows its `r-…` id. A seat no longer says that it handed work off, and it no longer restates, confirms or corrects what an approval card shows. No host check enforces that last rule: it is prompt text.

Replies no longer carry the "Sources read this turn: …" footer (OPE-2487). The sources line now goes to the `reply.provenance` audit row as `detail.sources`. The host still strikes any model line that starts with "Sources read this turn:". The misattribution note is now visible to operators only. `detail.sources` can keep a vendor record title (up to 160 characters) for the life of the audit row. When a person asks what the agent read, the model answers and the host does not check the answer. The seat prompt also gains a "Your voice" section and plain-words citations.

One outbound guard rewrites raw ids into words on every surface, with no switch (OPE-2482). It rewrites text and never refuses or drops a message. It rewrites scope keys (for example `slack/…` becomes `<#C…>` on Slack, or words such as "a Slack conversation" elsewhere), `oe-grant-…` ("another conversation"), `wrun_…` ("a session"), `mtg_…` ("the meeting"), Teams ids (`19:`, `29:`, `8:orgid:`) and bare Slack user and channel ids. It never turns a bare person id into a live mention. It leaves mentions, URLs, code and routing fields (button values, block ids) alone. The guard runs at each provider's write seam: Slack (cards included), Discord, Teams, GitHub, Linear and Notion comments, email and Google Chat. It does not cover eve's own Slack session-client posts, Discord thread titles, or the Notion pages and Linear issues that the agent writes. A lookup resolves at most 12 ids in 1.5 s per text, with a 30-minute cache. Audit rows keep the raw ids. The new seat tool `look_up` resolves a name. It joins the lean roster (now 18 names) and the worker read group, and each name it returns marks the turn as untrusted.

The chief-of-staff watch is on for every member (OPE-2422). Each member's own 1:1 DM turn writes a `personal_watch` row at the `less` dial. The Slack Home tab gains a "Your watch" section with More, Less and None buttons. `/oe watch more|less|none` works on every `/oe` surface. The new `personal-watch` schedule runs every 30 minutes. It reads nothing and sends no nudge until the app declares a source on a `personal: true` collector and registers a personal reader. Core ships no reader and no calendar connector. Until then, the Home tab and `/oe watch` say that the calendar is not connected. Admins see `personal_watch.silence`, `personal_watch.nudge`, `personal_watch.dial.set` and `personal_watch.response`. Expect one `personal_watch.silence` row for each held-back finding once a source is on.

Teams changes for every install. (1) The Teams front route answers 403 to an activity whose `channelId` is not `msteams` (OPE-2455). Bot Framework Web Chat, Direct Line and the Azure portal's "Test in Web Chat" now get 403. (2) A 1:1 chat with a roster member of the home tenant now binds as verified, and it reaches the `dm` memory layer (OPE-2446). Before, every Teams DM bound as external. A guest, a member of another tenant, or an install with no home tenant set stays unverified. The home tenant comes from the existing `MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID` or `TEAMS_TENANT_ID`. (3) `/oe` commands work on Teams, and the answer posts into the conversation, so the room sees it (OPE-2443). (4) The agent posts its intro once in each Teams channel: on the bot join, or on the first @mention in a channel with no intro marker (OPE-2444). Every channel of an existing install gets the intro on its next @mention. (5) An approval card for a Teams personal or group chat now posts in that chat (OPE-2447). Before, it went to a Slack or Discord room. Name-drop wake on Teams channels follows the existing domain field `nameDropWake` (OPE-2445), so a domain that set it now also wakes on Teams. Admins see `teams.intro_posted` and `teams.oe_command`.

A seat woken by a name-drop now answers a question or request that names it (OPE-2465). Before, it answered `no_reply`. This affects only a domain with `nameDropWake: true`. Trust grading, the fence and approvals do not change. The change is prompt text, and no live run proves it yet.

Core offers five new roster names: `channel/a2a-inbound` (OPE-2448), `hook/personal-watch-enroll` and `schedule/personal-watch` (OPE-2422), `tool/expect_bot_reply` (OPE-2426) and `tool/look_up` (OPE-2482). Until `oe build --accept` records them in `roster.lock.json`, the build reports them as unreviewed and `oe build --check` exits 1 (manual steps).

The operational store gains two tables: `personal_watch` (OPE-2422) and `meeting_data` (OPE-2461). An owner boot creates them on Postgres and on SQLite, with no migration script. Each has row-level security on Postgres. The runtime role gets `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` on `personal_watch` (no DELETE) and `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on `meeting_data`. A two-role Postgres deployment needs the owner boot first and then its runtime grants again (manual steps). Without the grants, watch enrolment fails quietly and is retried on the next turn.

The seat prompt changes in four commits (OPE-2465, OPE-2480, OPE-2487, OPE-2482). An app that overrides a shipped `instructions.md` must merge the new text, for example the paragraph that starts "Never write a raw id…".
manualSteps: Run `npx oe build --accept`, then commit `roster.lock.json`. It records the five new core names: `channel/a2a-inbound`, `hook/personal-watch-enroll`, `schedule/personal-watch`, `tool/expect_bot_reply` and `tool/look_up`. Without this step `oe build --check` exits 1.

On a two-role Postgres deployment (a separate non-owner runtime role), run ONE boot as the owner role BEFORE the runtime tier reaches 0.7.0. That boot creates `personal_watch` and `meeting_data`. Then run the statements `runtimeRoleGrantsSql("<runtime role>")` returns, as the owner (`docs/extending/database.md`, step 3). Without the grants the runtime role gets `permission denied` on the new tables. A one-role deployment and SQLite need no step.

Account for the new routes and the new schedule that every 0.7.0 install mounts: `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` and `POST /a2a/jsonrpc` (both answer 404 until you turn on inbound A2A), and the `personal-watch` schedule every 30 minutes. Update an edge allowlist or a cron budget that lists routes and schedules by name. An app that selects the Google Chat provider also gets `POST /eve/v1/google-chat`.

Update every saved search, alert or script that matches the old person-facing text. These no longer appear: "Sources read this turn:" (read `detail.sources` on the `reply.provenance` audit row); "Approval requested:" and the old card detail lines (read the Slack message metadata or the block id); the old `/oe status` labels; "I hit an error", "Task failed:", "deployment logs" and "Couldn't complete that:" (read the logs); routine notices with an `r-…` id; and raw ids, scope keys, `wrun_…` and `mtg_…` in the agent's posts. Audit rows, `STATUS.md` keys and routing values keep their old shape. Replace any app import of `approvalLabel` with `pendingCardLines`, `cardFooter` or `decidedCardLine`.

Teams: upload a new app package (manifest version 1.0.4) to get the compose-box command list for `/oe` (OPE-2443). No permission changes. Tell anyone who tests the bot through Web Chat or Direct Line that it now answers 403. To verify a home-tenant member's 1:1 chat, make sure `MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID` (or `TEAMS_TENANT_ID`) names the home tenant. Most installs set it already. Without it, Teams DMs stay unverified.
Optional — Slack: re-apply the manifest to show `watch [more | less | none]` in the `/oe` usage hint. No scope or event changes.

Optional — Google Chat as a surface (OPE-2442). Add `@open-everywhere/provider-google-chat` at 0.7.0 to the app's `package.json`, add `"google-chat": true` under `providers` in `roster.config.ts`, and run `npx oe build --accept`. Copy `agent/google-chat/policy.ts` from the 0.7.0 template and add `import "../google-chat/policy.js";` to `agent/lib/register-config.ts`. Do not copy the template's `register-config.ts` whole: an import of a missing package or policy file fails the boot. In Google Cloud, turn on the Chat API, create a service account with a JSON key, and set the Chat app's HTTP endpoint URL to `https://<deployment host>/eve/v1/google-chat`. Store the whole key with `npx oe secret set GOOGLE_CHAT_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY`. Then set `enabled: true`, `audience`, `workspace` and `internalDomainIds` in the policy by pull request. Put `google-chat/<workspace>/<space id>` in the owning domain's `reach`. Vouch for the space in `agent/identity/surfaces.ts`. Add the app to each space. The full list is `docs/deploy/surfaces/google-chat.md`. An @mention or a slash command in a space wakes the domain's seat, and an internal person's 1:1 DM wakes their DM seat. Google Chat shows no approval cards: a governed act goes to a card-capable room of the same domain. The surface does not support group chats, DMs from external senders, ambient messages, edits, reactions, files, routines or reading a space. No live e2e covers this surface yet. Without these steps nothing changes.

Optional — inbound A2A (OPE-2448). Copy `agent/access/a2a-inbound.ts` from the 0.7.0 template. In `agent/lib/register-config.ts`, import `assertA2aInboundDomains` and `registerA2aInbound` from `@open-everywhere/core/agent/a2a/inbound/declaration.js`, `registerA2aInboundPlatform` from `@open-everywhere/core/agent/a2a/inbound/platform.js` and `A2A_INBOUND` from `../access/a2a-inbound.js`. Call `registerA2aInbound(A2A_INBOUND)`, `assertA2aInboundDomains(A2A_INBOUND, loadDomains())` and `registerA2aInboundPlatform()` after `registerA2aAgents`, as the template does. Set `a2a: { inbound: true }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts` and declare at least one caller in a team domain. A caller authenticates with a JWT from a declared issuer or with a bearer secret that you store with `npx oe secret set <ref>`. A call lands as an unattended job bound external, so it reads only `public` memory. 🔴 It still holds every tool and connector grant of its domain, so declare a caller only in a domain whose grants you would expose to it. A revoked bearer secret can work for up to 60 s. The JWKS fetch does not go through the egress guard. See `docs/extending/a2a-agents.md`.

Optional — the chief-of-staff watch's first source (OPE-2422). In `agent/routines/collectors.ts`, declare a collector with `personal: true`, then add `registerPersonalWatch(PERSONAL_WATCH)` with a `PersonalWatchDecl` that names it (`detect: "calendar-conflicts"`), as the 0.7.0 template does. Register a reader with `registerRoutineCollectorReader(reader, { personal: true })`. Core ships no reader and no calendar connector. The boot refuses a source whose collector is not `personal: true`.

Optional — Okta Cross App Access sign-in for a personal connection (OPE-2453). Declare `signIn: { mode: "xaa", … }` on the server in `agent/access/mcp-servers.ts`. Each secret field is a credential-store ref that you set with `npx oe secret set`, and every endpoint must be https. The Okta setup and the field list are in `docs/capabilities/connectors-and-providers.md` § Cross App Access. No live Okta run proves this yet, and no vendor app documents a way to admit a self-hosted client today. Admins see `connector.xaa.link_refused`.

Optional — teach a task by demonstration (OPE-2454). It needs the personal browser from 0.6.0. Rebuild and republish the browser image from `deploy/personal-browser/`, because an older image has no recorder and `teach` refuses. A proposal opens a pull request through the skill-proposal path, so it needs the config repo, `memory.skillProposalPr` on, and `accessRequests.dryRun` off. A taught draft can hold labels from the person's sites, and the rehearsal sends GET requests in the signed-in session. Admins see `browser.personal.teach`.

Optional — a person's request to another bot in chat (OPE-2426). It needs `slackAsYou({ clientId })` in `agent/access/mcp-servers.ts`, and it works on Slack only. The DM seat posts the request in the person's name (an approval card each time) and admits the other bot's replies only in that thread, for at most 6 hours and 5 replies. The window can close early with no notice. Admins see `bot_ask.expected`, `bot_ask.refused` and `bot_ask.reply_relayed`.

Optional — you can now turn on meeting recaps (OPE-2461, OPE-2464). Do the meeting preparation from the 0.6.0 entry, build and publish the bot image, set `box.image`, add at least one `hosts` rule and set `enabled: true`. For recaps from the platform's own transcript, declare `native.teams`, `native.meet` or `native.zoom` and set `native.enabled: true`. Each meeting row now expires on its own (`retention.transcriptDays`), and the `meeting-sweep` schedule deletes expired rows first. A recap post marks every turn in its channel as untrusted for 7 days.

releases.summary: 🔴 0.6.0 IS A MINOR RELEASE BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT AN EXISTING INSTALL DOES. Read the breaking changes and the manual steps BEFORE you deploy. An app on 0.4.0 that upgrades straight to 0.6.0 must also read the 0.5.0 entry below. `oe upgrade` shows both. Four changes alter what an existing install does by default. First, a person's DM seat can now ask a domain they belong to (OPE-2452). The new DM tool `ask_domain` sends the question to that domain's standing seat, which answers under its own policy into the person's DM only. It is on for every declared domain on Slack (`dmQuestions`, default on). Second, a Slack approval card can now offer a third button, "Approve, and allow things like this" (OPE-2456). In the person's own DM a confirmed rule applies at once and shows under Your rules in the Home tab. In a domain room it opens a pull request against the app's new `agent/access/domain-rules.ts`. Plain Approve never writes a rule. Third, a deploy that changes ONLY your app's own code or config now retires every standing seat and work session (OPE-2466). Before, such a deploy rotated nothing, so the change never reached a live seat. Fourth, text that people read no longer shows raw ids (OPE-2462). DM footers, the grant card, many approval cards and `/oe budget` name people and places in words. After a personal sign-in, the job that asked for it resumes on its own. Two features are on after the deploy with no config. Any Slack person can opt out of agent actions on their own content with `/oe optout on` or the Home tab (OPE-2436). The Slack side panel lets a person talk to their own DM seat beside any channel (OPE-2457), and it needs the re-applied Slack manifest (manual steps). These features stay off until you declare them: the agent's own email address (the new package `@open-everywhere/provider-email`, OPE-2440); the person's own browser, which keeps their logins (OPE-2441); and the Teams admin-centre package (`surface_app_package`, OPE-2438). Meeting recaps ship but CANNOT be turned on yet: OE's own meeting bot (OPE-2459, OPE-2469), speech to text as a stack role (OPE-2470) and recaps from the platform's own transcript (OPE-2471). The policy refuses `enabled: true` until OPE-2461 and OPE-2464 land. You can ignore them for this upgrade. No environment variable is added or removed. The eve peer stays 0.71.0. The operational store gains three tables (`dm_rule`, `person_opt_out`, `personal_browser`). An owner boot creates them, and a two-role Postgres deployment must re-run its runtime grants.
breaking: A person's DM seat can now ask a domain's standing seat (OPE-2452). The DM-seat tool `ask_domain` reaches a domain when the person is a full member of the workspace and sits in one of the domain's internal rooms that has a running seat. That seat answers with `answer_domain_question` (a new name in the lean roster, which now holds 17 names), under the domain's own policy, and the answer goes to the person's DM only. The host does not stop the domain seat from posting in its own room. The delivery tells it not to. Only Slack registers a membership probe, so on other platforms `ask_domain` refuses. A pseudo-domain never answers. Each question writes `domain_question.*` audit rows on both sides. The new domain field `dmQuestions` turns it off for one domain (default on). A domain question is not covered by a person's opt-out yet: the domain seat can still save what was asked.

A Slack approval card can now carry "Approve, and allow things like this" between Approve and Reject (OPE-2456). The button shows only when all of these hold: `approvals.judgeMode` is `enforce` (the shipped value); the act can reach the judge (`open_pull_request`, a `create_routine` with no standing write, or a connector write or delete that passes every connector floor); the card did not freeze `tainted: true` (an `open_pull_request` or `create_routine` card must freeze `tainted: false`); and the room is the person's own Slack DM, or a Slack room of exactly one domain on a deployment with a config repo and an admin channel. The button opens a confirmation dialog with the rule in plain words. Code writes the rule from the card's frozen act. It never quotes an argument, and an instance lint refuses a rule that names one object. A DM rule lives in the new `dm_rule` table. It applies at once to its owner's asks in that DM only, at most 20 per person. The person removes it under Your rules in the Home tab. The judge now reads DM rules too, so a DM with a rule costs judge calls where it cost none. A domain rule opens a pull request that adds or widens one line of `agent/access/domain-rules.ts`. Nothing applies until an admin merges it. Teams and Discord cards do not show the button. Each step writes an `approval.rule.*` audit row.

The code fingerprint now has an app half (OPE-2466). `oe build` hashes your app's own tree (every `.ts` file except `.d.ts`, tests and `oe build` output, and every `instructions.md`, under `agent/`, plus `roster.config.ts`, `roster.lock.json` and `patches/`) and writes it to `agent/lib/app-code-fingerprint.generated.ts`. The generated provider table imports it, so no hand edit is needed. A deploy that changes only app code or app config (for example an A2A declaration or a bundle) now retires every standing seat and work session at its next wake. The per-domain declarations stay out of the hash, so a domain edit rotates nothing. The walk reads the disk, not git: an untracked `.ts` file under `agent/` in the build checkout gives one commit a second fingerprint. The first deploy of 0.6.0 rotates every seat and work session once.

Any Slack person can now opt out of agent actions on their own content (OPE-2436), with `/oe optout on|off` (a private answer) or a button in the Home tab. The switch keys on the acting person only, so nobody can set it for somebody else. While it is on: the host refuses every agent memory write attributed to that person; the dream cycle learns nothing from their turns; and the Slack message shortcut wakes nothing when somebody else presses it on their message. The person's own Edit and Forget, an approved purge and an admin edit still land. An unreadable store refuses the act. NOT covered: the person's words stay in the session, so a later turn by somebody else can save a fact from them; a fact about the person that somebody else states; Notion, Linear and GitHub objects the person created; and `/oe optout` on Discord. Admins see `person.opt_out.set`, `person.opt_out.cleared` and `person.opt_out.refused` in the audit log. The state lives in the new `person_opt_out` table.

Person-facing text names people and places in words, not raw ids (OPE-2462). This covers the DM footer ("You asked for this" for the asker, and no footer when the DM lands where the person asked), the grant card, the grant-use and room notices, the chat-DM card, the blocked ping, the DM refusals, most approval cards, the `/oe budget` replies and `describeTrigger`. The grant card no longer shows the principal key that OPE-1083 made visible. Update any saved search, alert or script that matched a raw id in these lines. When a job stops for a personal sign-in, the job resumes on its own once the person connects the account. When the sign-in card lands in the person's own DM, the seat no longer repeats what the card already said.

The Slack app manifest that `surface_manifest` and `/setup` return now turns on `features.agent_view` (the side panel, with a description and the `slack.suggestedPrompts`), adds the bot scope `assistant:write` and the bot event `app_context_changed`, and adds `optout [on | off]` to the `/oe` usage hint (OPE-2457, OPE-2436). An existing install keeps its old app until you re-apply the manifest and reinstall (manual steps). Until then the side panel does not appear. `/oe optout` works anyway. In the side panel a message wakes the person's own DM seat, with the same session and grants as the DM.
