The viewed channel's id reaches the seat as context only, and only when the person is a full member, the channel is in the same workspace and Slack confirms it internal. The seat gains none of that channel's reads.

The Teams app manifest's long description now names Microsoft Teams in full and says that the agent uses AI and that a reply can be wrong (OPE-2438). An existing Teams app shows the old text until you upload a new package. No scope or permission changes.

The operational store gains three tables: `dm_rule` (OPE-2456), `person_opt_out` (OPE-2436) and `personal_browser` (OPE-2441). An owner boot creates them on Postgres and on SQLite, with no migration script. Each has row-level security on Postgres. The runtime role gets `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE` on `person_opt_out` (no DELETE) and `SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE` on the other two. A non-owner runtime role runs no DDL, so a two-role Postgres deployment needs the owner boot first and then its runtime grants again (manual steps).
manualSteps: Re-apply the Slack app manifest on every EXISTING Slack app, then reinstall the app to the workspace so it takes the new scope. Run `surface_manifest` (or open `/setup`) and paste the manifest it returns, or make the changes by hand: turn on the agent view (`features.agent_view`), add the bot scope `assistant:write`, and add the bot event `app_context_changed`. The side panel needs all three (OPE-2457). Slack says some AI features need a paid plan. If the app ever had the older `assistant_view`, the move to `agent_view` cannot be undone, and people need a hard refresh. The Home tab from 0.5.0 must stay on: Your rules and the opt-out button live there.

Add `/agent/lib/app-code-fingerprint.generated.ts` to the app's `.gitignore` (OPE-2466). `oe build` writes that file on every build and warns while git does not ignore it. Build from a clean checkout, because an untracked `.ts` file under `agent/` changes the fingerprint, and every seat then rotates on a deploy that changed nothing. Expect the first deploy of 0.6.0 to start every standing seat and work session on a fresh generation.

On a two-role Postgres deployment (a separate non-owner runtime role), run ONE boot as the owner role BEFORE the runtime tier reaches 0.6.0. That boot creates `dm_rule`, `person_opt_out` and `personal_browser`. Then run the statements `runtimeRoleGrantsSql("<runtime role>")` returns, as the owner (`docs/extending/database.md`, step 3). Without the grants the runtime role gets `permission denied` on the new tables. A one-role deployment and SQLite need no step.

Account for the new routes and schedules that every 0.6.0 install mounts, whatever the meeting and browser policies say: `POST /meetings/v1/:id` (the meeting bot callback), `/browser/v1/view`, `/browser/v1/live` and `/browser/v1/live/*` (the personal browser watch page, which answers 404 without `OE_INTAKE_PAGE_SIGNING_KEY`), the `meeting-sweep` schedule every 15 minutes and the `personal-browser-sweep` schedule every 5 minutes. Update an edge allowlist or a cron budget that lists routes and schedules by name. `oe build --accept` adds them, and eight new tools, to `roster.lock.json`. An app that mounts the email provider also gets `POST /eve/v1/email`.

Decide which domains take questions from a member's DM (OPE-2452). To keep a domain out, add `dmQuestions: false` to that domain's `defineDomain` call in `agent/memory/config/domains/`. A domain that keeps the default answers its members' DM questions from the first deploy.

To take domain rules from approval cards (OPE-2456), copy `agent/access/domain-rules.ts` from the 0.6.0 `@open-everywhere/create` template into the config repo. In `agent/access/bundles.ts`, add `import { domainRuleBindings, domainRuleBundles } from "@open-everywhere/core/agent/access/domain-rules.js";` and `import { DOMAIN_RULES } from "./domain-rules.js";`, then `bundles.push(...domainRuleBundles(DOMAIN_RULES));` and `bindings.push(...domainRuleBindings(DOMAIN_RULES));` after the MCP server lines, as the template does. The domain path also needs the config repo and the admin channel in `agent/access/access-requests.ts`. Until then, a domain-room click on the rule button approves the act, writes no rule, and the card says that the file is missing. `npx oe upgrade --plan` lists the file as missing. DM rules need no step.

Optional — the side panel's suggested prompts (OPE-2457). Set `slack: { suggestedPrompts: [{ title, message }] }` in `SETTINGS_OVERRIDES` in `agent/settings/settings.ts` (at most 4), then re-apply the manifest. The three shipped prompts name no product. An empty list offers none.

Optional — an email address for the agent (OPE-2440). Add `@open-everywhere/provider-email` at 0.6.0 to the app's `package.json`, add `email: true` under `providers` in `roster.config.ts`, and run `npx oe build --accept`. Copy `agent/email/policy.ts` and `agent/email/senders.ts` from the 0.6.0 template, and add `import "../email/policy.js";` to `agent/lib/register-config.ts`. The first transport is AgentMail on a domain the org controls (MX, SPF, DKIM and DMARC records). Point its webhook at `https://<deployment host>/eve/v1/email`, subscribed to the four `message.received*` events, and store `AGENTMAIL_API_KEY` and `AGENTMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET` with `npx oe secret set`. Then set `enabled: true`, the inboxes and the allowed senders in the policy by pull request. Put a room inbox's key (`email/<domain>/<local>`) in a domain's `reach`, and a person's address in their principal's `ids.email` for the personal inbox. A room inbox in a multi-source window also needs a `defineSurface` entry in `agent/identity/surfaces.ts`. The gate admits only a sender whose mail passes DMARC. The full list is `docs/deploy/surfaces/email.md` § What an operator must provision. Without these steps nothing changes.

Optional — the person's own browser (OPE-2441). Copy `agent/personal-browser/policy.ts` from the 0.6.0 template and add `import "../personal-browser/policy.js";` to `agent/lib/register-config.ts`. Build and publish the browser image from `deploy/personal-browser/` in the Open Everywhere repository, set `box.image`, then set `enabled: true`. The browser works only in the person's own DM, and it reaches only the hosts the person's DM egress declaration admits. On docker the box opens only when the setting `egress.allowUnenforced` is declared, because docker cannot fence it and the box's own proxy is the only fence. The watch page needs `OE_INTAKE_PAGE_SIGNING_KEY` and a public URL, as the credential intake page does. Without these steps the tools refuse.

Safe to ignore for this upgrade — meeting recaps (OPE-2459, OPE-2469, OPE-2470, OPE-2471). The meeting policy refuses `enabled: true` and `native.enabled: true`, and the boot fails, until OPE-2461 and OPE-2464 land. To prepare, copy `agent/meetings/policy.ts` and add `import "../meetings/policy.js";` to `agent/lib/register-config.ts`. Copy `TRANSCRIPTION`, `LOCAL_TRANSCRIPTION`, `TRANSCRIPTION_PLACEMENT` and `resolveTranscription` (with its `TranscriptionRoleSpec` type import) into `agent/model/stacks.ts`, export `TRANSCRIPTION_ROLE` from `agent/model/models.ts` (add `resolveTranscription` to its `./stacks.js` import), and add the `registerGatewayMeetingModels(...)` line and its import to `agent/agent.ts` (with `TRANSCRIPTION_ROLE` in the `./model/models.js` import), as the 0.6.0 template does. The bot's transcript carries no speaker names yet. Only a recap from the platform's own transcript carries them.

Optional — a Teams app package for the Teams admin centre or the store (OPE-2438). Run the ops MCP tool `surface_app_package` with `route: "org"` (an admin uploads the zip in the Teams admin centre) or `route: "store"` (a publisher submits it in Partner Center). The store route makes you choose `channelFeatures`: `"omit"` (chats only) or `"tier1"` (channels, including shared and private channels, which are untested). Add `teams-app/*.zip` to `.gitignore`. A store listing can still fail one rule: the store wants an AI label visible in the chat, and OE's Teams replies carry none yet. Upload a new package to an existing Teams app to show the new long description.

Optional — the `american-closed` stack's vision role moved to `google/gemini-3.8-flash` in the template (OPE-2468). The price is unchanged. Your app's `agent/model/stacks.ts` keeps its own model. To follow, change the vision id there and the matching row in `agent/spend/model-pricing.ts`.

releases.summary: 🔴 0.5.0 IS A MINOR RELEASE BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT AN EXISTING INSTALL DOES. It replaces the unpublished 0.4.1 entry: an app on 0.4.0 upgrades straight to 0.5.0. Read the breaking changes and the manual steps BEFORE you deploy. Five changes alter what people see by default. First, a declared team domain that omits `mode` now shares ONE standing seat across its rooms (OPE-2412). Write `mode: "solo"` on a domain to keep the 0.4.0 shape. Second, a DM is now one conversation that carries on (OPE-2431). Every DM rotation carries a conversation summary of up to 32,000 tokens (`rotation.dmSummaryTokenCap`) beside the verbatim tail. A long DM therefore costs more per request and rotates sooner. Third, thread seats close on their own (OPE-2428). A thread with no message for 3 days closes, and every close hands a host-written report back to the parent. A thread that finishes with `complete_thread` gets ✅ on its root message on Slack. Fourth, every approval card opens with one plain sentence of what will happen and to whom (OPE-2434). On Slack, several asks from one job in one room and thread join one card. Fifth, Slack's status line now names the step while a turn works (OPE-2449), for example `Searching Notion…`. A shared room therefore sees which kind of tool and which vendor runs. Other changes are on after the deploy with no config. The Slack Home tab shows a person what the agent remembers about them, with Edit, Forget and Export (OPE-2451). A domain with memory also writes a canvas into its internal Slack channels. Both need the re-applied Slack manifest (manual steps). A work session or thread seat that reports itself `blocked` pings its person once in their DM (OPE-2433). The new DM-only tool `waiting_on_me` lists that person's open cards. A Teams channel now hosts its own approval card (OPE-2424); 0.4.0 sent the card to a Slack or Discord room. A domain that holds a Teams channel may need a Teams admin (manual steps). Automatic offboarding revokes a deactivated Slack member's link-set once the app receives `user_change` (OPE-2423). Per-tool usage analytics (OPE-2435) record every tool call in the new `tool_usage` table, from the first call after the deploy. No setting turns them off. These features stay off until you declare them: audit export to a SIEM (`auditExport.targets`, OPE-2437); an output language (`language.output` and a domain's `language`, OPE-2450); and webhook targets on Discord, Teams and a person's DM (OPE-2419). Three more stay off until you declare them: "search Slack as you" on the person's own sign-in (`slackAsYou`, OPE-2421); "set up X" from chat, which proposes an `agent/access/mcp-servers.ts` entry as a pull request (`propose_mcp_server`, OPE-2420); and outbound A2A delegation to declared agents (`agent/access/a2a-agents.ts`, OPE-2425). No environment variable is added or removed. The eve peer stays 0.71.0. The operational store gains two tables (`tool_usage`, `attention_state`) and one column (`pending_actions.group_key`). An owner boot creates them, and a two-role Postgres deployment must re-run its runtime grants. Three fixes also change behaviour. A config repo in dry-run mode now holds the skill proposal pull request and the directory-group overlay pull request too (OPE-2416). A thread seat's ownership now lasts 7 days from its last activity, not from its spawn. A static-confidential sign-in now sends its declared `scopes`.
breaking: An explicit (`reach`) domain that does not set `mode` now resolves `"unified"` when its reach is all exact keys, at least two rooms are left after its `windows` groups, and every such room passes the operator-vouch rule of a multi-source window. Each of its rooms then shares ONE standing seat and ONE session registry row (`oe-domain::<domain>`), in place of one seat per room. In 0.4.0 the same domain resolved `"solo"`. A domain that fails one of those conditions stays `"solo"`. The `org`, `public` and `dm` pseudo-domains and the `oe-dm/` DM seats stay solo.

A DM seat rotation now carries the DM's conversation summary beside the 5,000-token verbatim tail (OPE-2431). The summary holds the DM's most recent messages: at most 200 entries, each cut to 480 characters, capped by the new setting `rotation.dmSummaryTokenCap` (shipped 32,000 tokens by the characters-per-token proxy). No model writes it, and a refuted or ungraded author's message never enters it. The fresh generation holds the summary in context, so a long DM has up to 32,000 fewer tokens of headroom under `rotation.contextSizeTokens` (120,000) and adds up to 32,000 input tokens to each request against the DM token backstop: both rotate it sooner. Rough cost on the shipped stack for an active DM (20 turns a workday): about $1.35 a month before and $1.90 after. The summary is one row per DM seat in the existing `session_tail` table, under the reserved token `oe-dm-summary`. The next rotation replaces it, and nothing deletes it, a DM stop included. The first rotation after the deploy starts the summary from the outgoing generation's recorded messages, so a DM keeps nothing older than its current generation recorded. A channel seat is unchanged.

Thread seats close on their own (OPE-2428). The daily tidy sweep closes a thread seat whose thread has had no routed message for 3 days, with the reason `expired`. Every close (`completed`, `expired`, or `closed` by the ingress reap) now posts a host-written hand-back to the parent's live generation; the seat's own summary rides inside it when it wrote one. `complete_thread` posts the completion in the thread when the seat did not post that turn, and the host puts ✅ on the thread's root message on Slack, and on a Linear reply thread. A thread seat now survives its parent's rotation, and its ownership lasts 7 days from its last routed message, not from its spawn. A thread seat reads its own persona and is never offered a hand-off. A DM seat now reads a short DM persona, where 0.4.0 gave it none.

Every approval card on Slack, Teams and Discord opens with one plain sentence of what will happen and to whom (OPE-2434). The `Approval requested: <kind>` label moves to the second line. Code writes the sentence from the card's frozen arguments and removes link markup, mentions and `@everyone`/`@here` from each value. A bare URL stays as visible text, and the detail lines below the sentence are not cleaned. A saved search, alert or script that reads the card's first line as the label must read the second line now. On Slack, several asks from one job in one room and thread now join ONE card of at most five items, and each click still decides exactly one item. Teams and Discord still post one card per ask.

`update_status` now takes a typed state: `working`, `needs_input`, `blocked` or `done` (OPE-2433). The first `blocked` report of an episode sends the session's person ONE DM, on the new proactive-DM plane `attention.blocked`: the cleaned status line and a link to the work. The person's own stop outranks it. The host also cleans every status line (`linkSafeLine`) before it stores or sends it.

Slack's status line now shows a step label while a tool runs (OPE-2449): `Searching Notion…`, `Reading the PR…`, `Reading the channel…`. Code writes the label from the tool's name and, for a connector, from a fixed list of vendor names. It never shows a query, a page, a URL or a tool's output. Only a read, a search, sandbox code or a hand-off to a declared subagent gets a label; a write, the `reply` tool, a `grant__` tool and an unknown MCP server show the status verb as before. In a shared channel the label tells the room which kind of tool runs, and for a connector, which vendor. No setting turns it off. The reply still posts once, after every check.

The Slack app manifest that `surface_manifest` and `/setup` return now turns the Home tab on, adds the bot scope `canvases:write` and adds the bot events `app_home_opened`, `channel_shared` and `user_change` (OPE-2451, OPE-2423). When the app declares `slackAsYou` in `agent/access/mcp-servers.ts`, the manifest also adds the bot scope `mcp:connect`, the user scopes a person consents to, and the redirect URL `/oauth/v1/callback` (OPE-2421). An existing install keeps its old app until you re-apply the manifest (manual steps). Until then the Home tab and the canvas do not appear, each failure (`views.publish`, `missing_scope`) is logged and audited, and memory itself is unaffected.

A domain with memory now writes its memory as a canvas into its internal Slack channels that the app is in (OPE-2451). The app writes or rewrites the canvas at each memory write to one of the domain's silos. When a person joins a channel, or Slack shares it, the app checks the channel again and takes its canvas down if the channel fails the check. One refresh writes at most 20 channels in total, across all the domains that name the written silo. The app writes the canvas only into a channel that Slack confirms unshared. Every member of that channel must be a full member that `users.info` confirms, and a channel with more than 200 members is refused. The app never writes over a canvas a person made. When a channel stops passing these checks, the app replaces its own canvas with a notice that holds no memory. `memoryCanvas: false` on a domain turns the canvas off and takes the app's old canvas down at the next memory write or trust check. A wait for the canvas refresh adds at most 1.5 seconds to a memory write.

A Teams channel now hosts its own approval card (OPE-2424): an Adaptive Card with Approve and Reject, answered on the existing `/eve/v1/teams` route below the Bot Framework JWT check. In 0.4.0 the card went to a card-capable Slack or Discord room in the same domain. A tap counts only from `channelId: "msteams"` with a tenant. An admin-tier card needs a `teams/<29:id>` entry on `Domain.admins`. A Teams team owner is not an approver on that standing alone. A domain whose `admins` lists only Slack or Discord people therefore has nobody who can tap an admin-tier card in its Teams channel. A Teams personal or group chat still sends its card to a card-capable channel. `declare_webhook` cards are refused on a Teams tap. The support matrix cell is 🔧 until a live leg passes.

A webhook `target` (in `agent/webhooks/hooks.ts` and in `declare_webhook`) now takes a room on Slack, Discord or Teams (`slack/T…/C…`, `discord/<guild>/<channel>`, `teams/<tenant>/<conversation>`) or a person's DM (`dm:slack/T…/U…`, `dm:discord/<user>`, `dm:teams/<29:id>`) (OPE-2419). A Slack channel target behaves as in 0.4.0. Every other target binds `external`. A Slack DM target fires only to a full member of the named workspace. On Discord and Teams a webhook fails closed: a group chat or group DM is refused, a channel fires only when `agent/identity/surfaces.ts` declares it internal (`defineSurface`), and a 1:1 DM fires. A target that cannot resolve declines with a `webhook.declined` audit row that names the fix.

A Slack `user_change` event that reports a deleted member now revokes that person's link-set and purges its stored logins (OPE-2423). Five gates fail closed: the account is in the workspace whose signed envelope delivered the event, config names that workspace, a live `users.info` confirms the deactivation, only a confirmed link revokes the set, and a set that also holds the person's account on another workspace or platform is never revoked whole. Each report writes one audit row. Teams has no automatic leg.

`accessRequests.dryRun: true` now holds EVERY config-repo write (OPE-2416). The skill proposal pull request (`memory.skillProposalPr`, on since 0.4.0) and the directory-group overlay delivery opened real pull requests on a dry-run install in 0.4.0. Now each audits the attempt with `dryRun: true` and opens no branch and no pull request.

Per-tool usage analytics ship on (OPE-2435). The `tool-usage` hook writes one row per finished tool call, and `requestApproval` writes one row per posted card, into the new append-only table `tool_usage`. Each row holds ids and counts: the org, the surface, the principal id, the session id, the tool, the connector and op, the outcome, the model and an even share of the model step's tokens. It never holds the call's input or output. The tokens are attributed, not measured. Three new reads expose the rows: the `tools` dataset of `query_analytics`, the control MCP tool `tool_usage`, and the control route `GET /control/v1/tool-usage` (a service token from `OE_CONTROL_READ_TOKENS`; 404 when none is set; self-audited). No setting turns the recording off, and no prune deletes the rows.

A static-confidential sign-in (`oe-oauth`) now sends the `scopes` its declaration names on the authorize URL. 0.4.0 dropped them. An MCP server whose sign-in is static-confidential (a `clientId` and a `clientSecretRef`) and declares `scopes` therefore asks a person for those scopes at the next sign-in. A discovery (DCR) sign-in already sent its scopes.

The operational store gains the append-only table `tool_usage` (OPE-2435), the table `attention_state` (OPE-2433) and the column `pending_actions.group_key` (OPE-2434). An owner boot creates them on Postgres and on SQLite, with no migration script. A non-owner runtime role runs no DDL, so a two-role Postgres deployment needs the owner boot first and then its runtime grants again (manual steps).
manualSteps: Decide, BEFORE you deploy, which declared domains share one window. To keep a domain's rooms in their own seats as in 0.4.0, add `mode: "solo"` to that domain's `defineDomain` call in `agent/memory/config/domains/`. A domain that already writes `mode` does not change. Each domain that takes the new default opens a fresh shared seat at the first wake after the deploy, and the per-room seats it replaces get no new wake.

Decide the domain memory canvas BEFORE you re-apply the Slack manifest. Once the app holds `canvases:write`, every domain with memory writes a canvas into its internal Slack channels at its next memory write. To keep a domain's memory out of its channels, add `memoryCanvas: false` to that domain's `defineDomain` call in `agent/memory/config/domains/`.

Re-apply the Slack app manifest on every EXISTING Slack app, then reinstall the app to the workspace so it takes the new scope. Run `surface_manifest` (or open `/setup`) and paste the manifest it returns, or make the changes by hand: turn on the Home tab under App Home; add the bot scope `canvases:write`; add the bot events `app_home_opened`, `channel_shared` and `user_change` under Event Subscriptions. The memory page and the domain canvas need the first three changes (OPE-2451). Automatic offboarding needs `user_change` (OPE-2423): without it, a deactivated member keeps their link-set and stored logins until an admin runs `revoke_link_set`, as in 0.4.0. The app already holds `users:read`, `channels:read` and `groups:read`.

On a two-role Postgres deployment (a separate non-owner runtime role), run ONE boot as the owner role BEFORE the runtime tier reaches 0.5.0. That boot creates `tool_usage`, `attention_state` and `pending_actions.group_key`. Then run the statements `runtimeRoleGrantsSql("<runtime role>")` returns, as the owner (`docs/extending/database.md`, step 3). They grant `SELECT, INSERT` only on `tool_usage` and the verbs `attention_state` needs. Without the grants the runtime role gets `permission denied` on the new tables. A one-role deployment and SQLite need no step.

If a DM's cost matters more than its memory, lower `rotation.dmSummaryTokenCap` in `agent/settings/settings.ts` (shipped 32,000). A lower cap carries fewer of the DM's recent messages across a rotation. The rotation backstops are unchanged.

Check the code that reads approval cards. A Slack, Teams or Discord card's first line is now a plain sentence, and the `Approval requested: <kind>` label is the second line. Update any saved search, alert or script that matched the first line.

If your control plane sits behind an edge allowlist, or the deployment has a retention policy, account for `GET /control/v1/tool-usage` and for the `tool_usage` rows. Each row names a principal id and a session id, and nothing prunes the table.

If a domain that holds a Teams channel uses admin-tier cards, add each Teams admin as `teams/<29:id>` (the Bot Framework id) to that domain's `admins` BEFORE you deploy. Until then, nobody can tap such a card in Teams, and only the control plane (`decide_pending_action`) can decide it. No Teams manifest change is needed: the bot answers `Action.Execute` itself. Until a live tenant leg passes, treat the Teams card as built and unit-tested only.

Optional — send the audit log to a SIEM (OPE-2437). Add `auditExport: { targets: [{ name, format, url, tokenSecret }] }` to `SETTINGS_OVERRIDES` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`. `format` is `"otlp"`, `"json"` or `"splunk-hec"`; `url` is `https:` (or an `http:` loopback collector). `tokenSecret` is the NAME of a secret (for example `SPLUNK_HEC_TOKEN`): store its value with `npx oe secret set <NAME>`, never in the environment, because the exporter reads the secret store only. The `audit-export` schedule sends every row after the target's cursor every 5 minutes, AT LEAST ONCE: deduplicate on `(org, seq)` in the SIEM. A bad entry fails the boot. `docs/deploy/siem-export.md` gives the formats and the chain check.

Optional — set an output language (OPE-2450). Add `language: { output: "<BCP 47 tag>" }` (for example `"fr"` or `"pt-BR"`) to `SETTINGS_OVERRIDES`, and a domain's own `language` to override it. An explicit domain without one inherits the `org` domain's value; `dm` and `public` do not. A bad tag fails the boot. Card text, slash-command output and other host-rendered text stay in English.

Optional — delegate to other agents over A2A (OPE-2425). Copy `agent/access/a2a-agents.ts` from the 0.5.0 `@open-everywhere/create` template. In `agent/lib/register-config.ts`, add `import { registerA2aAgents } from "@open-everywhere/core/agent/a2a/agents.js";` and `import { A2A_AGENTS } from "../access/a2a-agents.js";`, and call `registerA2aAgents(A2A_AGENTS);` before `registerConfig(...)`, or sync that file from the template. Then declare each agent by its `https` card URL; a bearer token is a credential-store REF (`npx oe secret set db:a2a:<name>`), never a value. Without these edits `delegate_to_agent` reaches no agent. Each delegation needs an approval: a member's click on a card, or a pre-approval rule or the approval judge that lifts it. Only an internal room may delegate. The answer is untrusted content. `docs/extending/a2a-agents.md` states the limits.

Optional — "set up X" from chat (OPE-2420). In `agent/access/access-requests.ts`, add `import { MCP_SERVERS } from "./mcp-servers.js";` and the line `baseMcpServers: () => MCP_SERVERS,` in the returned config, or sync that file from the 0.5.0 template. `propose_mcp_server` also needs the admin channel and the config repo configured in that file. Without them it refuses and tells the person that an admin adds the entry by hand. A merged entry reaches every person who can DM the agent unless `people.groups` narrows it.

Optional — "search Slack as you" (OPE-2421). In `agent/access/mcp-servers.ts`, import `slackAsYou` from `@open-everywhere/provider-slack/agent/slack-as-you.js` and add `slackAsYou({ clientId: "<your Slack app's Client ID>" })`. Store the app's Client Secret with `npx oe secret set db:slack:oauth-client-secret`. Re-apply the manifest that `surface_manifest` then returns (`mcp:connect`, the user scopes, the `/oauth/v1/callback` redirect), and turn on the MCP toggle in the Slack app's Agents section by hand: the manifest has no field for it. The connection works only in the person's own Slack 1:1 DM, and every post as the person takes a card. Live consent on a real workspace is not yet proven: `docs/deploy/surfaces/slack.md#search-slack-as-you` lists what is unconfirmed.

Optional — a webhook into Discord, Teams or a DM (OPE-2419). Write the new `target` shape in `agent/webhooks/hooks.ts`. Before a Discord or Teams CHANNEL target can fire, declare that channel internal in `agent/identity/surfaces.ts` (`defineSurface`). A Discord or Teams group chat is refused.

releases.summary: 🔴 0.4.0 IS A MINOR RELEASE BECAUSE IT CHANGES WHAT AN EXISTING INSTALL DOES. Read the manual steps BEFORE you deploy. Five things change. First, many shipped defaults flip on: the ambient supervisor, standing seats, connectors in channels with a card per write, personal logins in DMs, the routine card wait and the skill proposal pull request. The external-participant policy also ships strict. The first two manual steps give the edits that keep the 0.3.0 defaults. Two changes have no settings key: the approval judge may lift a connector delete, and an MCP server's tool annotations help decide an op's tier. The manual steps on `agent/access/pre-approval-rules.ts` and on MCP servers say how to hold each one at a card. Second, 45 environment variables stop working. A behaviour choice moves into `agent/settings/settings.ts`, `agent/access/access-requests.ts` or a connector's connection module. A tuning knob becomes a code constant. Two switches that only a test deployment uses move into `agent/settings/settings.ts`, and the other test valves leave the environment. The manual steps map each variable to the line that replaces it, or say that it has no replacement. Third, five features are deleted with no replacement: the failure digest's draft pull request, the DM seat's quiet-gap rotation, the `audit` settings group, the `requestorEntitlementChecks` domain flag with its entitlement probe, and Vercel Blob HTML hosting. Fourth, an admin declares MCP servers in the app's own `agent/access/mcp-servers.ts`, and a DM uses the asking person's own login. Fifth, on self-host behind the egress proxy, you rebuild the proxy with the app, and the `docker` sandbox backend refuses to boot once `agent/sandbox/sandbox.ts` is synced from the 0.4.0 template. The details follow. 🔴 THE AMBIENT SUPERVISOR IS NOW ON BY DEFAULT (OPE-2409), AND AN UPGRADE TURNS IT ON. Before this release a domain's `ambientSupervisor` flag had to be literally `true`, so an app that never set it was ADDRESSED-ONLY everywhere: the agent woke on a mention or a name-drop and nothing else. From this release an unset flag inherits the `org` domain's value, and an unset `org` flag means ON. After the upgrade, every unaddressed message or comment on an ambient-capable surface wakes that room's ambient supervisor session (its standing seat once `window.topology` is armed), which judges it and replies or stays silent. What that reaches, per surface: on Slack, every channel or private group the bot is in that the workspace positively confirms internal (never a DM, never an externally-shared or unconfirmable channel); on GitHub, every positively private or operator-vouched repo the app is installed on; on Linear, every team the app can see, whatever its privacy; on Notion, every page the integration can see, INCLUDING a page in no explicit domain, which was silent in 0.3.0 and which runs at `external` trust unless a trust root or vouch covers it. Discord and Teams do not read this flag, and nothing changes there. A surface in no explicit domain on an app with NO `org` domain stays off. To keep the 0.3.0 behaviour, set `ambientSupervisor: false` on the `org` domain BEFORE you deploy (see the manual steps). The flag lifts no fence: the per-surface checks above, the author and trust checks, the tenant fence and the spend caps still apply as before. A quiet room costs nothing. Each unaddressed message costs one judged turn on the `supervisor` model route, and a silent verdict is still a paid turn. Three built capabilities now ship on (the house default: a built, proven capability ships on unless a concrete reason forbids it). `approvals.routineCardWaitSeconds` ships 120 where it shipped 0: an unattended routine fire that its permission card refuses now holds the refusing call for up to 120 seconds, so a person who is around can approve the card while the run is still up. The wait is still clamped to what the turn can afford, and a deadline never decides the card. `memory.skillProposalPr` ships `true` where it shipped `false`: a skill proposal now also opens a pull request on the config repo wherever the deployment configures `accessRequests.configRepo`. With no config repo the proposal stays in the review queue, as before, and nothing errors. A new app from `@open-everywhere/create` sets `browser: { enabled: true }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`, beside the `localhost` and `127.0.0.1` rows its browser host declaration already carries, so a worker can boot the app it changed and screenshot it on a Vercel deploy. The framework default of `browser.enabled` stays `false`, because core declares no browser host. The browser runs on the Vercel Sandbox backend only: on Docker or another self-host the plane refuses, mounts no tool, opens no host and logs one line that names the platform. The external-participant policy also ships strict: `externalPolicy.authorGrain` is `"withhold"` and `externalPolicy.roomGrain` is `"silent"` (see the breaking items for what changes and how to opt out). Three unused features are deleted by OPE-2410, so the shipped tree is smaller. The weekly failure digest loses its last-mile arm, which opened a draft pull request with a repro for the top cluster. The arm shipped off, and no production code registered its repro transport or its approval gate. The digest itself is unchanged: it still posts the top clusters to the access-requests admin channel. A DM seat loses its quiet-gap rotation trigger, `OE_DM_SEAT_ROTATE_QUIET_GAP_HOURS`. It shipped off, and a DM seat keeps its expiry clock and its turn, token and context-size rungs. The `audit.silences` setting is deleted. No setting or environment variable arms the judged-silence rows `unified.no_reply`, `reply.no_reply` and `reply.no_reply_redundant` now, so core never writes them on its own. The always-on `reply.no_reply_observed` and `turn.bare_stop` rows are unchanged. The `requestorEntitlementChecks` flag on the `org` domain is REMOVED, with the connector-disclosure leg it armed. Core never shipped an entitlement probe, so with the flag set to `true` and no probe registered it refused every directly-addressed connector call. It also contradicted the rule that a turn runs as its ROOM, never as a person. The disclosure gate now judges the room only: its audience floor and its roster read. A deployment that still sets the key gets a boot error that names it. Delete the key. An app that never set it needs one edit only: delete the `assertComplianceDomains` import and call from `agent/lib/register-config.ts`. Vercel Blob HTML hosting is removed. `post_file` attaches an HTML page as a downloadable file, which is now its only behaviour. Nothing is ever published to a public URL, and `post_file` raises no approval card. Three shipped defaults move. Connectors are no longer DM-only: `connectors.opTiering` ships `true` and `connectors.dmOnly` ships `false`, so a channel reaches a connector exactly when a domain or bundle grants it, a read runs with no card, and a write or a destructive op gets a card that approves one call. The approval judge may pre-approve a write or a recognised delete under a bound pre-approval rule. Standing seats are on: `window.topology` ships `true`, so every channel the bot is in gets its own solo seat, and the `org` catch-all stays solo. A shared window exists only where the deployer declares one (an explicit `unified` domain or a named `windows` group), and the quickstart skill now offers one `unified` domain as an optional step. An app that already declared the new values can delete those entries. The approval judge may now approve a connector delete, and an org-admitted MCP server's own tool annotations now help decide how consequential each of its operations is. A connector op whose name carries a recognised delete verb now reaches the judge on the same code floors as a write: the domain's own credential, an attended turn that read no external content, a room with exactly one domain, and an input the card shows in full. An op whose name carries no recognised verb (`execute_sql`) is fail-closed `destructive`, not a known delete, and it keeps its card. This replaces the earlier rule that every delete stays a person's call. Which deletes the judge lifts is the deployer's pre-approval rules. The template ships a new strict starter rule, `connector-delete-asked-for-here`: it covers only a delete of exactly one item that the requester named, in their own words, in this turn, and never a bulk or wildcard delete. The starter `connector-write-asked-for-here` rule now says that it never covers a delete. Separately, the connector seam reads each registered MCP server's `readOnlyHint` and `destructiveHint` annotations. Where the op name carries no verb the classifier recognises, the hint decides, so a read with an unusual name can run with no card. Where the name carries a known verb, the stricter of the two wins. An op with no hint and no recognised verb stays `destructive`, and a `connectorOps` raise still applies on top of a hint. The `connector.op` audit row carries `opTierHint`, and `opTierHintDecided` when the hint moved the tier. A connector card now freezes the op's effective tier as `opTier`, which the judge reads. A write-named op that a `connectorOps` raise or a server annotation made destructive keeps its card. The judge never caches an allow for a connector op, so an identical later call is judged again. The verb lists are unchanged: a longer read list would also open every unknown mutation spelled beside a read verb, so an unusual read is opened by its server's `readOnlyHint` instead. Personal logins are the DM default, and an app can declare its own MCP servers (OPE-2414). `connectors.userPrincipal` and `connectors.linkSetVault` ship `true`: in a DM, a connector call uses the asking person's own account, a person who has not signed in gets the "Connect my account" card, and one consent covers all of a person's linked accounts. Channels keep the org credential paths unchanged, a personal-credential write in a shared room stays refused, and the member plane stays off. A new app file, `agent/access/mcp-servers.ts`, declares an MCP server in a few lines: its URL, a description, and its sign-in (MCP OAuth discovery and dynamic client registration by default; a static client id and a secret REF only for a vendor without dynamic registration). `oe build` writes the connection for each entry, and every person reaches the server in their own DM as themselves. A channel gets nothing until an admin grants the server's `workspace-oauth` credential on a bundle. A person in chat cannot add a server: the list changes by pull request only. Self-host egress (OPE-2406, OPE-2407). On the Docker Compose stack, the app's own model call now reaches the model gateway through the ENFORCING egress proxy. The proxy decides a request that carries the proxy token against a host plane that holds the gateway host only. It decides a request with no token against the session's own policy, as before. A proxy built before this release answers the app's host-plane push with a 400, and the model call then fails closed, so rebuild the proxy with the app. The `docker` sandbox backend starts each session container on the Docker daemon's default network, outside the proxy. So `sandbox.selfHostBackend: "docker"` together with `OE_EGRESS_PROXY_URL` now refuses to boot, once the app's `agent/sandbox/sandbox.ts` is synced from the 0.4.0 template. The root `Dockerfile` builds again, and the compose stack boots (OPE-2193). `oe upgrade --from <dir>` rehearses an upgrade from `npm pack` tarballs before a release is published (OPE-2355). The browser tools work again on eve 0.69 and later: before this release every `browser_*` call threw before it ran (OPE-2403). With no `identity.name`, the default avatar is now the project mark (OPE-2408). The Teams app package ships the mark as its two icons, and the setup guides tell you to upload `brand/png/mark-square-1024.png` where a surface takes its icon by hand.
breaking: `ambientSupervisor` defaults to ON. An explicit domain that does not set it now inherits the `org` domain's value, and an `org` domain that does not set it means ON. In 0.3.0 an explicit domain never inherited the flag, and an unset flag anywhere meant OFF. So an upgrade turns the ambient supervisor on in every Slack, GitHub, Linear and Notion room whose domain does not write `ambientSupervisor: false`, within each surface's own floor (see the summary). On Notion this includes every page the integration can see that no explicit domain names. A 0.3.0 app that set `org: { ambientSupervisor: true }` and left an explicit domain unset ALSO changes: that domain now inherits `true`. The one exception is a surface in no explicit domain on an app with no `org` domain at all: it stays off, and its skip row reads `no-domain`.

An `ambient_skipped` audit row (`github.`, `linear.` and `notion.ambient_skipped`) with reason `no-domain` now means only that no domain can route the surface: no explicit domain names it AND the app has no `org` domain, or the domain set did not load. A surface in no explicit domain on an app WITH an `org` domain is no longer skipped for that alone: it inherits the `org` domain's flag. A `domain-refused` row names the domain that routes the surface, and adds `declaredBy` when the `false` came from the `org` domain instead.

The external-participant policy ships strict. `externalPolicy.authorGrain` ships `"withhold"` (it was `"taint"`), and `externalPolicy.roomGrain` ships `"silent"` (it was `"engage"`). An EXCLUDED author is one the surface refutes (a Slack guest or stranger, a Teams guest, a GitHub commenter that is not `OWNER`, `MEMBER` or `COLLABORATOR`, a Linear workspace guest) or one the author-trust register refutes (Discord and Notion). An excluded author can no longer task the agent, and their text reaches the model only as the arrived-marker. One known limit stays: on Discord, an excluded author quoted in the hydrated context behind a member's trigger still reaches the model. An excluded author's @mention or DM gets the private notice or the one-line ack on Slack, Discord, Teams, GitHub and Linear. On Notion nothing is posted. A room the classification calls external (a room declared `public`, a Slack Connect or Teams shared channel, or a wake whose trigger author is refuted) is silenced. It posts at most one join notice and one suppressed-wake notice, ever, and an @mention there gets the one-line ack. A member's own new messages are not withheld, and a room that no leg classifies external is never silenced. Three changes still reach members. First, a guest's text in an internal room reaches the model as the arrived-marker, in a wake and in `read_channel`/`read_thread`. Second, a session-tail row recorded before OPE-1747 carries no author grade, so `withhold` shows it as the arrived-marker, a member's row included, until newer rows replace it. Third, Slack's native `app_mention` forward and the Teams pre-ack gate now buy a per-author membership probe on every wake, which the old pair skipped.

`defineSettings` takes no `audit` group. An app that keeps `audit: { silences: … }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts` gets a type error, and `defineSettings` also refuses the unknown `audit` group when the module loads, so the app does not boot. Delete the group. No setting or environment variable arms the judged-silence rows `unified.no_reply`, `reply.no_reply` and `reply.no_reply_redundant` now. To see why the agent stayed quiet, read the session transcript (`GET /control/v1/session/:id/transcript`).

The subpath export `@open-everywhere/core/agent/memory/dream/mode3-last-mile.js` is removed, with `MODE3_LAST_MILE`, `registerMode3Repro`, `registerMode3LastMileApproval` and `runLastMile`. `mode3Tick` takes no `lastMile` option, and `formatMode3Report` takes no `footer` argument. `@open-everywhere/core/agent/memory/dream/mode3.js` no longer exports `FACET_LABEL_MAX` or `FACET_SKETCH_MAX`. An app that imports one of them must delete the import and the code that uses it. There is no replacement. The `dream.mode3_report` audit row no longer carries a `lastMile` field, and nothing writes `dream.mode3_last_mile`.
`ConfigPrProvider.openOrReopenPr` takes no `draft` argument. Only the deleted last-mile arm passed it. A self-hosted provider can keep the field, but core never sets it.

`Domain` has no `requestorEntitlementChecks` field. A domain that sets it fails typecheck, and an untyped config that sets it fails boot: `assertDomainsValid` refuses the key BY NAME, for `true` and `false` alike. Delete the key. A boot error is the kinder choice than a silent drop: the flag only ever refused, so a silent drop would widen what that deployment discloses and say nothing.

`@open-everywhere/core/agent/memory/domain.js` no longer exports `assertComplianceDomains` or `requestorEntitlementChecksEnabled`. `@open-everywhere/core/agent/access/connector-disclosure.js` no longer exports `registerConnectorEntitlementProbe`, `ConnectorEntitlementProbe` or `ConnectorEntitlementError`. `ConnectorDisclosureInput` has no `complianceMode`, `directAddressed`, `entitled`, `entitlementDetail` or `opTier`, and `ConnectorDisclosureVerdict` has no `requestor-unentitled` or `entitlement-unavailable` arm. A probe that an app registered is gone with no replacement: connector reads are judged on the room, never on the person who asked.

The disclosure gate no longer writes the audit action `connector.entitlement_check`, and `connector.refused` no longer carries the reasons `requestor_unentitled` or `entitlement_unavailable`. Old rows stay in the log. A saved query or alert on those names now matches nothing new.

Vercel Blob HTML hosting is removed. `post_file` attaches an HTML page as a downloadable file, which is now its only behaviour. It never publishes a page to a public URL and never posts a `file.publish` card. These are gone with it: the `file.publish` approval kind, the `AppConfig.loadBlobHosting` member, the `setBlobPutter` and `BlobPutter` exports of `@open-everywhere/core/agent/adapter-api.js`, the subpath exports `@open-everywhere/core/agent/blob/hosting.js`, `@open-everywhere/core/agent/approvals/file-publish.js` and `@open-everywhere/adapters/agent/blob/hosting.js`, and the `@vercel/blob` dependency of `@open-everywhere/adapters`. An app that imports one of them gets a type error. Delete the import and the code that uses it. There is no replacement.

`connectors.opTiering` ships `true` and `connectors.dmOnly` ships `false`. An app that declares neither now lets a channel reach every connector a domain or bundle grants it: a read runs with no card, and a write or a destructive op gets a card that approves one call. The approval judge may pre-approve a write or a recognised delete under a bound pre-approval rule. Before, a non-DM connector call was refused with `dm_only`. To keep connectors in DMs only, declare `connectors: { dmOnly: true, opTiering: false, userPrincipal: false }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`. Arming `dmOnly` alone changes nothing while `opTiering` is on. The `connector.use` audit row now stamps `grant: "work-surface"` on every resolved non-DM call, not only where the wall was up.

`window.topology` ships `true`. An app that declares nothing now gives every channel the bot is in its own standing seat (`solo`): a mention lands in the room's own seat, not in a fresh per-thread session. The gate also arms mid-session memory re-sync org-wide, which propagates deletes into the sandbox. The `org` pseudo-domain stays solo, and the boot still refuses `mode` on it. An app that declares no `org` pseudo-domain keeps the native per-container path for an undeclared channel. To keep the old path everywhere, declare `window: { topology: false }`.
`connectors.userPrincipal: true` with no `opTiering` key now boots, because `opTiering` ships on. The boot still refuses `userPrincipal: true` together with `opTiering: false`.

OPE-2411: twenty-four behaviour environment variables are deleted, and nothing reads them now: `OE_MODEL_STACK`, `OE_PRIMARY_MODEL`, `OE_FORCE_MODEL`, `OE_ADMIN_GITHUB`, `OE_ADMIN_ROLE_RULES`, `OE_ALLOW_MULTI_TENANT_PRINCIPALS`, `OE_TRUST`, `OE_TEAMS_SERVICE_HOSTS`, `OE_TIDY_ORGS`, `OE_DIRECTORY_AUTOCONFIRM`, `OE_DIRECTORY_GROUP_ALLOWLIST`, `OE_DIRECTORY_OKTA_APPS`, `OE_AWS_ENABLED`, `OE_AWS_SSO_SCOPES`, `OE_MEMORY_SYNC_TIMING`, `OE_SANDBOX_BACKEND`, `OE_PLATFORM`, `OE_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_MEMORY`, `OE_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_OPERATIONAL`, `OE_ACCESS_DRY_RUN`, `OE_CREDENTIAL_BINDING_LIVE`, `OE_OAUTH_ENABLED`, `OE_OAUTH_CONFIG` and `OE_OAUTH_NOTION_RESOURCE`. Each value now lives in committed config: a row of `agent/settings/settings.ts`, a field of `agent/access/access-requests.ts`, or a connector's sign-in declaration. A deployment that set one and does not move it falls back to the shipped default with no error — for most of them that is the SAFER posture (a wall back up, a flag off), but a deployment that relied on `OE_ADMIN_GITHUB` or `OE_ADMIN_ROLE_RULES` loses that admin access, and one that relied on `OE_SANDBOX_BACKEND=justbash` off Vercel gets the `docker` backend. The manual steps name the line that replaces each variable.

The host is a fact, not a choice. `platformName()` answers `vercel` exactly when Vercel's own `VERCEL` is set, else `self-host`, and no `OE_PLATFORM` override moves it. The `OE_PLATFORM=vercel` route (a non-Vercel host running the Vercel Sandbox) is now `sandbox.useVercelSandbox: true`, and it no longer applies the Vercel durable-store floors to that host: the floors follow the real host. The browser plane, the egress apply path and the turn-end stop now read the SANDBOX (`resolveSandboxBackend`), so no environment variable can arm the browser plane on a host whose sandbox cannot run it.

The built-in OAuth flow always registers: there is no `OE_OAUTH_ENABLED` master flag. A connector declares its own sign-in in its connection module, next to its URL, with `declareConnectionSignIn` (new on `@open-everywhere/core/agent/adapter-api.js`), and the vault reads the declarations per call. The shipped Notion connection declares hosted Notion MCP's sign-in under the home ref `mcp.notion.com/notion-mcp`, so a deployment whose bundles grant Notion's `user-oauth` or `workspace-oauth` credential now offers the OAuth flow for it with no env var. A mint for an OAuth home no connection declares fails closed and names the fix, unless the vault already holds a client record or an unexpired token for that home: a stored row keeps serving. So deleting `OE_OAUTH_ENABLED` does not switch off a home that already has signed-in people; to switch one off, remove its `user-oauth` credential from the bundle, and no mint reaches the flow. `oeOauthEnabled` and `OE_OAUTH_CONFIG_ENV` are removed from `@open-everywhere/adapters/agent/oe-oauth/config.js`, `loadOeOauthConfig` takes a declaration map, and `registerOeOauth` no longer throws when nothing is declared.

Settings API: `getSettings(overrides?)` takes no `env` argument (it was `getSettings(env, overrides)`), `SettingSpec` has no `env` or `parseEnv` field, `SettingDoc` has no `env` field, and `settingEnvNames` is removed from `@open-everywhere/core/agent/settings/settings.js` and the adapter-api barrel. An app that calls `getSettings(process.env, SETTINGS_OVERRIDES)` (the 0.3.0 template's `agent/model/models.ts` does) gets a type error: call `getSettings(SETTINGS_OVERRIDES)`.

Renamed or reshaped exports. `MULTI_TENANT_ENV` is now `MULTI_TENANT_SETTING` (its value is the setting path). `OE_DIRECTORY_AUTOCONFIRM_ENV` is now `DIRECTORY_AUTOCONFIRM_SETTING`, and `directoryAutoConfirm()` takes no argument. `OE_DIRECTORY_GROUP_ALLOWLIST_ENV` is removed, and `directoryGroupAllowlist()` takes no argument. `OE_MEMORY_SYNC_TIMING_ENV` is now `MEMORY_SYNC_TIMING_SETTING`. `resolveSelfHostBackendKind` takes the `sandbox` settings group, not an environment. `parseOktaAppMap` is replaced by `oktaAppMappings(entries)`, and `loadOktaDirectoryConfig` takes the app table as a second argument. `decideStoreWiring` takes the `storage.allowEphemeralOperational` value as a third argument. `defaultAgentModelId` takes an optional `models` settings group. `assertSingleTenantPerTenantScopedPlatform` takes an optional second argument, the resolved `identity.allowMultiTenantPrincipals`.

A context with no channel no longer takes its platform from the environment: `channelPlatform` answers from the channel kind only. A unit test that used `OE_PLATFORM=slack` to route a channel-less context to a mapper calls the new test seam `setPlatformStandInForTest("slack")` from `@open-everywhere/core/agent/identity/binding.js`.

Nineteen environment variables are no longer read (OPE-2411). Thirteen were tuning knobs, and each is now a code constant at the value it defaulted to, so a deployment that set one of them gets the default. Six were test valves, and no environment variable arms a test seam any more. A test bed that set `OE_TEST_WAKE` or `OE_TEST_DRIVER_IDS` must move the value into `agent/settings/settings.ts` before it deploys, or the test-wake route answers 404 and the e2e driver bot is dropped. See the manual steps.

`connectors.userPrincipal` ships `true` (OPE-2414). In a DM whose bundles bind a `user-oauth` credential, a connector call now mints the asking person's own token. A person who has not signed in gets the "Connect my account" card. Before, the call was refused, because the app-principal path takes no personal credential. Channels are unchanged. To opt out, declare `connectors: { userPrincipal: false }`. That restores the refusal: it does not put DM calls on an org account, and every server declared in `agent/access/mcp-servers.ts` then refuses in a DM.

Because `userPrincipal` ships on, the boot now refuses `connectors: { opTiering: false }` declared ALONE: the resolved posture is the OPE-1319 hole (a personal credential in a DM with no per-op tiering). Declare `userPrincipal: false` beside it. The DM-only opt-out is now `connectors: { dmOnly: true, opTiering: false, userPrincipal: false }`.

`connectors.linkSetVault` ships `true` (OPE-2414). A confirmed link-set member now keys the user-OAuth vault by the set, so one consent covers all of that person's linked accounts. A token a person consented to under one account before the upgrade is keyed by that account, so a person in a link-set signs in once more. Arming the vault also suppresses directory auto-confirm for every link-set, so an app that sets `directory.autoConfirm: "attested"` confirms no link-set by itself any more: a person confirms each link. To keep the 0.3.0 behaviour, declare `connectors: { linkSetVault: false }`.

`oe:everyone` is a reserved person-group name: `assertGroupsValid` refuses a declared group with that name. It is the built-in group of every attested person, matched only in their own DM, and a `group` binding may name it without a registry entry. The broad-grant lint calls a credentialed `oe:everyone` binding broad, so it needs `allowBroad`.

The approval-site allowlist entry for connections moves from `packages/core/agent/connections/notion.ts` to `packages/core/agent/connections/mcp-server-connection.ts`, the one builder every MCP connection now uses. `notion.ts` builds through `buildMcpConnection` and no longer imports `defineMcpClientConnection`, `selectConnectorTransport` or `declareConnectionSignIn` itself. Its runtime behaviour is unchanged.

Self-host: `sandbox.selfHostBackend: "docker"` (the shipped default off Vercel) together with `OE_EGRESS_PROXY_URL` now refuses to boot (`DOCKER_BEHIND_PROXY_FATAL`). The refusal is in the app's own `agent/sandbox/sandbox.ts`: the 0.4.0 template throws on the `fatal` that `selfHostEgressBootLog()` returns. A `sandbox.ts` from 0.3.0 or earlier never reads `fatal`, so it logs `posture = refused` and boots, and the session container keeps its direct route out. The docker backend starts each session container on the Docker daemon's default network, with no proxy settings, so the proxy cannot enforce that session's egress. In 0.3.0 the pair booted, and the audit said "enforced" while the session container had a direct route out. The docker backend with no proxy is unchanged: it applies a coarse `deny-all`, and a session that needs a host allow-list aborts.

Self-host: on its first model call, the app pushes a host plane (`POST /policy` with `plane: "host"`) to the egress proxy. A proxy built from a release before 0.4.0 answers that push with a 400, and the app's model call then fails closed. Rebuild the proxy from this release's `deploy/egress-proxy` together with the app.

configMigrations.description: In `agent/settings/settings.ts`, delete each entry that now equals the shipped default: `window: { topology: true }`, `connectors.dmOnly: false` and `connectors.opTiering: true`. A no-op override hides the default it restates. Keep an entry only for a value that differs.
In `agent/settings/settings.ts`, delete `connectors.userPrincipal: true` and `connectors.linkSetVault: true` if you declared them: both now equal the shipped default (OPE-2414).

manualSteps: Decide, BEFORE you deploy, which new defaults you take. To keep the 0.3.0 behaviour of every default that flipped, add this to `SETTINGS_OVERRIDES` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`: `approvals: { routineCardWaitSeconds: 0 }, memory: { skillProposalPr: false }, externalPolicy: { authorGrain: "taint", roomGrain: "engage" }, connectors: { dmOnly: true, opTiering: false, userPrincipal: false, linkSetVault: false }, window: { topology: false }`. Merge each group into the group of the same name if the file already declares it. Then set `ambientSupervisor: false` on the `org` domain, as the next step says. Two changes have no settings key. The approval judge may now lift a connector delete under a pre-approval rule, and a server's tool annotations now help decide an op's tier: the steps on `agent/access/pre-approval-rules.ts` and on MCP servers say how to hold each one at a card. To take a new default instead, leave its key out. The steps below explain each default one by one.

Decide, BEFORE you deploy this release, whether your rooms become always-on teammates. To keep every room addressed-only as in 0.3.0, add `ambientSupervisor: false` to the `org` domain (`agent/memory/config/domains/org.ts` in a scaffolded app). Every explicit domain that does not set the flag inherits that `false`. If 0.3.0 had `ambientSupervisor: true` on `org`, that line alone does not restore 0.3.0: write `ambientSupervisor: false` on each explicit domain that left the flag unset, because in 0.3.0 those domains were off. To turn it on for most rooms and keep a few addressed-only, leave `org` unset and add `ambientSupervisor: false` to the domains of those rooms.

Check that the `org` domain routes `models.supervisor` to the model you want the ambient seat to run. The scaffold routes it to the stack's cheap supervisor tier at `low` reasoning. Unset, the supervisor route falls back to `primary`, and every judged ambient turn then runs on the primary model.

Decide the routine card wait. An app that sets no `approvals.routineCardWaitSeconds` now waits up to 120 seconds on an unanswered routine permission card before the run refuses. A routine run can then take up to two minutes longer before it reports. To keep the immediate refusal, set `approvals: { routineCardWaitSeconds: 0 }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`.

Decide the skill proposal pull request. An app that sets no `memory.skillProposalPr` and configures a config repo (`accessRequests.configRepo`) now gets a pull request on that repo for each skill proposal, on a `skill-proposal/` branch. The cycle never merges it. To keep the proposal in the review queue only, set `memory: { skillProposalPr: false }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`. An app with no config repo sees no change.

Decide the browser, if the app deploys to Vercel. The upgrade does not change `agent/settings/settings.ts`, because the app owns it, so an existing app keeps the browser off. To take the new template's default, add `browser: { enabled: true }` to `SETTINGS_OVERRIDES` and check that `agent/access/browser-hosts.ts` declares the `localhost` row (sync it from the 0.4.0 template if it does not). On Docker or another self-host, leave the browser off: the self-host image ships no Chromium, so the plane refuses there. A new app scaffolded at 0.4.0 that deploys to Docker can set `browser: { enabled: false }` to turn it off and to silence the boot line.

Decide the external-participant policy before you deploy this release. The new defaults are `withhold` and `silent`. To keep the old behaviour, set `externalPolicy: { authorGrain: "taint", roomGrain: "engage" }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`, or set one field only to opt out of one grain. To opt out for one domain, set `externalPolicy` on that domain in `agent/memory/config/domains/<name>.ts`; it resolves field by field over the org default. Check each room the deployment declares `public` in `agent/identity/surfaces.ts`: the agent is silent there from this release on, unless that room's domain sets `roomGrain: "engage"`.
Delete the `audit` group from `agent/settings/settings.ts`, if the app declares one. `defineSettings` refuses it, and the app does not boot until it is gone.
Remove `OE_DM_SEAT_ROTATE_QUIET_GAP_HOURS` from the deployment's environment, if it is set. Nothing reads it now: a DM seat never rotates on idleness alone.

Delete the `assertComplianceDomains` import and its `assertComplianceDomains(loadDomains());` call from `agent/lib/register-config.ts`, or sync that file from the 0.4.0 `@open-everywhere/create` template. Without the edit, the app fails typecheck on the missing export.
If a domain in `agent/memory/config/domains.ts` sets `requestorEntitlementChecks`, delete the key. Boot refuses it otherwise.

Delete `agent/blob/hosting.ts`, and delete the `loadBlobHosting` import and the `loadBlobHosting,` line from `agent/lib/register-config.ts`. Hosting is gone, and the app does not typecheck with either. Nothing reads `BLOB_STORE_ID` any more. Disconnect the Vercel Blob store if nothing else uses it.

A `file.publish` card that is still pending in the room does nothing when somebody clicks it, because its kind is no longer registered. It publishes nothing and expires at its TTL. Tell the room to ask again, and the agent attaches the page as a file.

Optional: declare ONE explicit `unified` domain if a few rooms should share one conversation. The 0.4.0 template's `agent/memory/config/domains/index.ts` and `.claude/skills/quickstart-open-everywhere/SKILL.md` show the shape. A fresh install declares none.

Read your app's `agent/access/pre-approval-rules.ts`. The judge now reads every rule against a connector delete as well as a write, so a rule that says only "a connector change" can now lift a delete. To keep every delete on a card, add the sentence "This rule never covers a call that deletes, removes, trashes or erases anything." to each connector rule, as the template's `connector-write-asked-for-here` now does. To let the judge lift a delete the requester named, copy the template's `connector-delete-asked-for-here` rule.

Check which MCP servers your app registers in `agent/connections/`. A server that declares `readOnlyHint: true` on a tool whose name the verb classifier does not recognise now runs that tool with no card. To hold such a tool at a card, name it under `gated` in a bundle's `connectorOps`.

OPE-2411 — move each retired environment variable your deployment sets into the config line that replaces it, then delete the variable from the env store (it does nothing now). In `agent/settings/settings.ts`: `OE_MODEL_STACK` → `models: { stack }`; `OE_PRIMARY_MODEL` → `models: { primary }`; `OE_FORCE_MODEL` → `models: { force }`; `OE_ADMIN_GITHUB=1` → `control: { githubAdmin: true }`; `OE_ADMIN_ROLE_RULES` → `control: { adminRoleRules: [...] }` (the same rules as a typed literal; a rule with no matcher now fails the boot); `OE_ALLOW_MULTI_TENANT_PRINCIPALS=1` → `identity: { allowMultiTenantPrincipals: true }`; `OE_TRUST=internal` → `identity: { blanketTrust: "internal" }`; `OE_TEAMS_SERVICE_HOSTS` → `teams: { serviceHosts: [...] }`; `OE_TIDY_ORGS` → `schedules: { sweepOrgs: [...] }`.

OPE-2411 — the directory, AWS and measurement choices. In `agent/settings/settings.ts`: `OE_DIRECTORY_AUTOCONFIRM` → `directory: { autoConfirm }`; `OE_DIRECTORY_GROUP_ALLOWLIST` → `directory: { groupAllowlist: [...] }`; `OE_DIRECTORY_OKTA_APPS=slack/T0AB1CD2E:0oa1:userName,…` → `directory: { oktaApps: [{ platform: "slack", tenant: "T0AB1CD2E", appId: "0oa1", field: "userName" }, …] }` (an upper-case platform token is now refused, not lower-cased); `OE_AWS_ENABLED=1` → `aws: { enabled: true }`; `OE_AWS_SSO_SCOPES` → `aws: { ssoScopes: [...] }` (keep `openid`); `OE_MEMORY_SYNC_TIMING=1` → `memory: { syncTiming: true }`.

OPE-2411 — the platform floors. In `agent/settings/settings.ts`: `OE_SANDBOX_BACKEND` → `sandbox: { selfHostBackend }` (an app built into the root Docker image must declare `"justbash"`: the image carries a just-bash template only, and the image no longer sets the variable); `OE_PLATFORM=vercel` on a non-Vercel host → `sandbox: { useVercelSandbox: true }`; `OE_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_MEMORY=1` → `storage: { allowEphemeralMemory: true }`; `OE_ALLOW_EPHEMERAL_OPERATIONAL=1` → `storage: { allowEphemeralOperational: true }`. `OE_PLATFORM=self-host` on Vercel has no replacement: the floors it lowered are the two `storage` rows. Then sync `agent/sandbox/sandbox.ts` and `agent/sandbox/backend-select.ts` from the 0.4.0 template, so the app builds its backend from `resolveSandboxBackend`. Without that sync the app and core disagree: the old `sandbox.ts` still builds a self-host backend, while core reads `sandbox.useVercelSandbox` and arms the browser plane, skips the egress proxy push and names Vercel as the stop owner. Do not declare `sandbox.useVercelSandbox` until both files are synced. This repository's own `agent/settings/settings.ts` declares `sandbox: { selfHostBackend: "justbash" }` for its Docker image and its integration tier, so a deployment made from a clone of this repository that runs off Vercel without that image must delete the entry to keep the contained `docker` default.

OPE-2411 — the access-request and OAuth choices. In `agent/access/access-requests.ts`, replace `dryRun: process.env.OE_ACCESS_DRY_RUN === "1"` with `dryRun: false` (a test bed writes `true`), and add `credentialBindingLive: false` (write `true` where the deployment set `OE_CREDENTIAL_BINDING_LIVE=1`). Delete `OE_OAUTH_ENABLED`, `OE_OAUTH_CONFIG` and `OE_OAUTH_NOTION_RESOURCE`: hosted Notion MCP's sign-in is declared by the shipped Notion connection. A provider your `OE_OAUTH_CONFIG` declared for another connector moves into that connector's own connection module as `declareConnectionSignIn("<home ref>", { … })`, keyed by the same home ref; a `static-confidential` entry keeps its `clientSecretRef`, never the secret.

OPE-2411 — two app files the 0.3.0 template generated. In `agent/model/models.ts`, call `getSettings(SETTINGS_OVERRIDES)` (no `process.env`) and pass the resolved `models` group to `defaultAgentModelId(...)`, or sync the file from the 0.4.0 template; it does not typecheck otherwise. In `agent/memory/config/domains.ts`, pass `getSettings(SETTINGS_OVERRIDES).identity.allowMultiTenantPrincipals` as the second argument of `assertSingleTenantPerTenantScopedPlatform(domains, …)`, or sync the file: that call runs before `registerSettings`, so without the argument a declared opt-in is not seen and the boot refuses two tenants.

Remove the thirteen retired tuning variables from the deployment's environment, if any is set. Nothing reads them now, and each is a code constant at its old default: `NOTION_VERSION` is `2022-06-28`; `OE_NOTION_MAX_PAGES` is 200, `OE_NOTION_MAX_DEPTH` is 6 and `OE_NOTION_TTL_MS` is 300000; `OE_LOG_SHIP_BATCH_MAX` is 20 and `OE_LOG_SHIP_FLUSH_MS` is 1000; `OE_WEBHOOK_MAX_BODY_BYTES` is 262144 and `OE_WEBHOOK_MAX_SKEW_SECONDS` is 300; `OE_EGRESS_DENIAL_POLL_MS` is 60000; `OE_SUPERVISOR_BACKSCROLL_REACHBACK_HOURS` is 168; `OE_DM_SEAT_ROTATE_EXPIRY_DAYS` is 30, `OE_DM_SEAT_ROTATE_TURN_BUDGET` is 50 and `OE_DM_SEAT_ROTATE_TOKEN_BUDGET` is 5000000. A deployment that set a different value loses it. A self-host `docker-compose.yml` copied from an earlier release can drop its `OE_EGRESS_DENIAL_POLL_MS` line.

On a test bed that set `OE_TEST_WAKE`: set `wake: { testWakeRoute: true }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts` and remove the variable. The route still needs the `OE_CONTROL_INJECT_TOKENS` credential, exactly as before. A real deployment leaves the setting off. This repository's own `agent/settings/settings.ts` turns `wake.testWakeRoute` and `wake.driverAllowlist` on for the maintainers' test bed, so a deployment made from a clone of this repository must delete those two entries.

On a test bed that set `OE_TEST_DRIVER_IDS`: move each comma-separated pair into `wake: { driverAllowlist: ["<guildId>:<botUserId>", "<teamId>:<botId>"] }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`, one string per pair, and remove the variable. A malformed pair now fails the boot instead of being dropped. Remove `OE_TEST_DRIVER_IDS` from the Discord relay's environment too: the relay now forwards a foreign bot's guild message to the deploy, and the deploy admits only a listed pair and drops every other bot message silently.

In test code that set `OE_EGRESS_SPOOF`, `OE_SCRIPTED_MODEL` or `OE_MEMORY_EVAL`: arm the matching in-process test valve instead, with `__setTestValveForTest("egress-spoof" | "scripted-model" | "memory-eval", true)` from `@open-everywhere/core/agent/testing/test-valves.js`. A separately started local process arms a valve with a preload instead: the local eval target that the window and solo e2e packs drive starts with `NODE_OPTIONS="--import=$PWD/packages/core/scripts/eval/arm-egress-spoof.mjs"`, or its replies post for real; a process that serves the memory battery uses `arm-memory-eval.mjs` the same way. Code that set `OE_ALLOW_TEST_NETWORK` passes its own `deps.read` to `hydratePointer` instead: the opt-out is gone.

To keep the 0.3.0 posture, add `connectors: { userPrincipal: false, linkSetVault: false }` to `agent/settings/settings.ts` BEFORE you deploy. With `userPrincipal` off, a DM's `user-oauth` binding is refused, as in 0.3.0: no DM call moves to an org account, and a server declared in `agent/access/mcp-servers.ts` refuses in every DM. To keep only one of the two, declare only that key.
If `agent/settings/settings.ts` declares `connectors: { opTiering: false }`, add `userPrincipal: false` beside it, or the boot refuses the settings.

To declare MCP servers in an app scaffolded before 0.4.0, copy `agent/access/mcp-servers.ts` from the `@open-everywhere/create` template. Then merge its entries in two files: in `agent/access/connector-credentials.ts`, `catalogues.push(...mcpServerConnectorCredentials(MCP_SERVERS))` before the first `assertConnectorCredentialsValid`; in `agent/access/bundles.ts`, `bundles.push(...mcpServerBundles(MCP_SERVERS))` and `bindings.push(...mcpServerBindings(MCP_SERVERS))` before the overlays merge. Both helpers come from `@open-everywhere/core/agent/connections/mcp-servers.js`. Then run `npx oe build`. An app with no `agent/access/mcp-servers.ts` declares no server, and `oe build` plans no connection for one.

On self-host behind the egress proxy (`OE_EGRESS_PROXY_URL` set), do four things before you deploy. First, rebuild the proxy image from this release's `deploy/egress-proxy` together with the app: `docker compose up --build` rebuilds both. An older proxy refuses the app's host-plane push, and every model call fails. Second, declare `sandbox: { selfHostBackend: "justbash" }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`, or the app refuses to boot on the shipped `docker` default. To keep the `docker` backend instead, remove `OE_EGRESS_PROXY_URL`: docker then applies only a coarse `deny-all`, and a session that needs a host allow-list aborts. Third, sync `agent/sandbox/sandbox.ts` from the 0.4.0 template, or add `if (egressLog.fatal !== undefined) throw new Error(egressLog.fatal);` after its `selfHostEgressBootLog()` call. Without that line the app boots on `docker` behind the proxy, and the proxy cannot fence the session. Fourth, in a `docker-compose.yml` copied from an earlier release, add `neon-wsproxy` to the app's `NO_PROXY`. Without it, Node 24 sends the op-store WebSocket through the proxy, the proxy denies it, and the app exits at boot.

releases.summary: The cross-surface window loses its question road and its tappable approval card, because no shipped session could reach them (OPE-2389). This is the breaking change, and the reason for a minor release. Since 0.2.0 no shipped production session on that window can raise a native input request: a conversation seat holds no `ask_question`, the work session holds only `agent` and `task_cancel`, a worker of the work session asks with `ask_room`, and no shipped tool raises a native `tool-approval`. The window now drops such a request and writes one `turn.question_dropped` audit row. The row is an alarm, not a fence: eve can still take that session's next plain message as the answer, without OE's admission check. The Notion question return is unchanged. Most apps need to do nothing about this: the breaking items touch only an app that imports one of the removed names or declares its own post arm. The ops MCP server no longer takes a secret value in a tool call (OPE-2396). The person types each secret into their own terminal with the new `npx oe env set <NAME>` (a hidden prompt, written to `.env.local`), and the agent handles names only. A running ops server also refuses every call once the installed core has a different version, and names both versions and the restart. `oe upgrade` now works across an eve peer change (OPE-2395): before the install it drops the `package-lock.json` entries of `eve` and of every `@open-everywhere/*` package, so npm no longer exits ERESOLVE. It prints a `DELETE` line for a file that a release removed from the template, and it reads `.oe-template-ignore` for the files the app owns. It also offers the starter pre-approval rules to an app that has none (OPE-2400). `@open-everywhere/core` no longer depends on `patch-package` (OPE-2398). The `oe-eve-patch` bin applies the eve patch itself, with the same rules and the same result, so a fresh app's `npm audit` no longer reports the `braces` advisory that came with it. An admin key can name the Slack Enterprise Grid: `slack/E<grid-id>/<member-id>` admits that person in every workspace whose delivery names that Grid (OPE-2400). A workspace key never reaches a sibling workspace. With `approvals.judgeMode: "enforce"` and no bound rule, the boot logs one line that says every gated act asks a person. `/setup` names the host it writes into the Slack manifest, and warns when that host answers a request with no cookie by a 401, a 403 or a redirect (OPE-2397). The deploy docs now say what a public custom domain exposes and how to close it. The scaffolder stops on a Node version below core's `engines.node`, and `create <name>` refuses a nested directory of the same name (OPE-2399). `npx @open-everywhere/create --check --host <url>` reads the env verdicts that the deployment reports for itself. The template ships `scripts/goldens/roster-plan.txt`, and its README, AGENTS.md, `.env.example` and setup skill state that runtime telemetry is on by default and how to turn it off. The telemetry default is unchanged. A one-shot routine that fails now says that its one scheduled fire failed, never "after 1 consecutive failures". The host composes that notice and no longer copies the model's declared reason into it (OPE-2394).
breaking: `@open-everywhere/core/agent/adapter-api.js` no longer exports these 24 names: `APPROVAL_BUTTON_LABELS`, `APPROVAL_CARD_REFUSED_AUDIT_ACTION`, `APPROVAL_CARD_SETTLED_AUDIT_ACTION`, `ApprovalCardInputResponse`, `ApprovalCardRespondFn`, `ApprovalCardTapOutcome`, `ApprovalCardTicket`, `ApprovalClickAuditReason`, `ApprovalClickDeps`, `ApprovalClickRefusal`, `ApprovalClickRouting`, `AttachSessionForRespond`, `OE_INPUT_CLICK_PREFIX`, `approvalCardActions`, `approvalCardRespondVia`, `approvalClickId`, `auditApprovalCardTap`, `forgetApprovalCardTicket`, `mintApprovalCardTicket`, `parseApprovalClickId`, `readApprovalCardTicket`, `rememberApprovalCardTicket`, `resolveApprovalCardClick`, `unifiedActionCapablePlatforms`. The subpath exports `@open-everywhere/core/agent/channels/approval-card.js`, `@open-everywhere/provider-slack/agent/channels/slack-approval-card.js` and `@open-everywhere/provider-discord/agent/channels/discord-approval-card.js` are removed too. They served the tappable approval card on the cross-surface window, which no shipped session could raise. An app that imports one of them must delete the import and the code that uses it. There is no replacement.

`PostArm` has no `dispatchUnifiedActions` member, and `postUnifiedReply` takes no `actions` argument. A post arm that an app declares itself must delete its `dispatchUnifiedActions` member. Core never calls it.

These types and signatures are narrower: `OutstandingQuestion` has no `optionIds`, the `answer` arm of `InboundAnswerRouting` has no `optionId`, its `wake` arm has no `addressed-mention` or `unmatched-option` reason, `resolveInboundAnswerRouting` takes no `text` or `addressedMention` input, `renderQuestionForSurface` takes one argument, and `UnifiedWindowWake` has no `followUp` field. A caller that passes one of them gets a type error. Delete the argument or the field.

The cross-surface window no longer writes the audit actions `turn.question_bridged`, `input_response.card_settled` and `input_response.card_refused`. `turn.question_dropped` now records every native input request that window receives, with `reason` `no-question-road` (or `work-session` for the work session). `input_response.routed` and `input_response.dropped` now come only from the Notion question return. A dashboard or an alert that counts these actions must change.

A Slack or Discord click whose action id starts with `oe_input:` is no longer handled by Open Everywhere. It goes to eve like any other click that is not ours. No shipped session posted a card that carries this prefix.

The ops MCP server (`open-everywhere-ops`) takes no secret value in any tool call. `scaffold_env` accepts `values` only for the six non-secret config names that it lists, and its schema refuses any other name. A secret goes in the new `secretNames` input; the reply gives the person's command `npx oe env set <NAME>` for each name and says whether the file already holds a value. `secret_set` takes `names` where it took a `secrets` map of name to value, and reads each value from the gated env file. A script or a prompt that passes a secret value to either tool must change. The `preflight` fix lines name the same command.

`@open-everywhere/core` has no `patch-package` dependency, and `@open-everywhere/core/agent/publish/eve-patch-pack.js` no longer exports `patchDirArgument`.
