The `oe-eve-patch` bin and `postinstall: oe-eve-patch` work as before. An app whose own scripts run `patch-package` must declare it in its own `devDependencies`, because core no longer installs it.
manualSteps: Run `npx oe build --accept` and commit `scripts/goldens/roster-plan.txt`, next to `roster.lock.json`. `oe upgrade` runs it for you; after a manual install, run it yourself. The file lists one line per slot file that `oe build` writes, with the package that mounts it, so a pull request shows what the agent gains or loses. Read its diff with the lock's, and never edit it by hand. `npx oe build --check` fails when the file differs from the plan.

Sync these template files from the 0.3.0 `@open-everywhere/create` template: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.env.example`, `.claude/skills/quickstart-open-everywhere/SKILL.md` and `.claude/skills/upgrade-open-everywhere/SKILL.md`. The app owns its scaffolded files, so `oe upgrade` changes none of them. `npx oe upgrade --plan` lists every file that differs. They carry the secret route (`npx oe env set <NAME>`, no secret in a tool call), the telemetry disclosure, the `--host` env verdicts and the golden file.
Restart every running ops MCP server (restart the coding agent session that holds it). A server that started on an older core keeps the old tool inputs and carries no stale-core guard.

Decide the telemetry setting. The deployed app sends anonymous usage telemetry, on by default, and the default is unchanged. To turn it off, set `OE_TELEMETRY=off` (or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`) on the deployment itself, in the Vercel project or the container environment. A value in `.env.local` reaches only a local run.

Check the approval judge, if the app has no `agent/access/pre-approval-rules.ts`. With `approvals.judgeMode: "enforce"` and no bound rule, every gated act asks a person, and the boot now logs a line that says so. `npx oe upgrade` and `npx oe upgrade --plan` offer the target template's starter rules and never write them. To take them, read each rule, copy the file, and bind it at org scope as the template's `agent/access/bundles.ts` does. To keep a card for every gated act, set `approvals: { judgeMode: "off" }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`.

Change any dashboard or alert that counts the audit actions `turn.question_bridged`, `input_response.card_settled` or `input_response.card_refused`. The cross-surface window no longer writes them; `turn.question_dropped` replaces them there.

releases.summary: The first published 0.2 release. 0.2.0 was never published to npm, so an app on 0.1.5 upgrades straight to 0.2.1 and acts on the 0.2.0 entry first: every breaking change, config migration, env removal and manual step there applies. 0.2.1 then fixes the 0.2.0 work and approval roads. An approved connector write runs the exact call that its card stored, named by the card id, and never an input the agent builds again. An `op.connector` card therefore stores the whole input of its call, up to 32,768 characters of key-sorted JSON, in its pending-action row in the operational store. The row keeps that input only while the card can still replay. A reject, an expiry, a replay that ran, or a spend by an identical call clears it, and the daily tidy clears what is left, which includes every card approved more than 25 hours ago. The preview, the input's digest and the decision stay on the row for the audit trail. A replay is refused once its write has run, so the write never runs twice. A card whose input is larger, or a card minted before 0.2.1, keeps the old road: after the Approve, the decision wake tells the job that asked to call the op again with the same input, and says that the act has not run yet. A follow-up after an Approve continues the task that its job names, so one approval no longer posts a second card. A follow-up that the work session refuses now reaches the room as a failed result, with one `work.request_refused` audit row, where it was lost before. An Approve or Reject click on a Discord DM card now wakes the DM seat. On Windows, the memory store retries a file rename that a concurrent reader blocks.
manualSteps: Carry out every item of the 0.2.0 entry, if the app is on 0.1.5 or earlier. No app ran 0.2.0, because it was never published, so none of its items is done yet. `npx oe upgrade` reads every entry between the installed version and the target from the target's record and prints them oldest first, so the 0.2.0 items come first.

releases.summary: 0.2.0 was never published to npm. Install 0.3.0 or later, and read the 0.2.1 entry too: an upgrade from 0.1.5 crosses this entry first, then the 0.2.1 entry. Every 0.2.0 change ships in 0.2.1 and later, so where this entry names a 0.2.0 deployment, package or template, read the version you install. The eve peer moves to 0.71.0, and every conversation runs on three tiers: the conversation seat answers the room and never waits, the conversation's own work session runs the jobs, and a worker does each job. Approvals and sign-ins are OE cards, a routine fire is a work request, and the agent's names and slash command come from the `identity.*` settings.
breaking: The eve peer is 0.71.0, where 0.1.5 declared 0.54.3. `oe upgrade` pins the app's `eve` to exactly `0.71.0`, and at install `oe-eve-patch` applies core's `patches/eve+0.71.0.patch` to it. An app that pins another eve version fails `oe-eve-patch` at install.

No session in flight at the deploy moves to the 0.2.0 deployment. eve refuses a session handoff across this boundary in both directions (the eve 0.69.0 and 0.70.0 changelogs). The owning 0.1.x deployment keeps running such a session, a worker's job included, for as long as that deployment is available: the job runs to its end under the old code, spends, and can post its result late into the room. Each standing seat rotates at its next wake (the next item), so the old session gets no new message, and the 0.2.0 seat knows nothing of the old job. A rollback from 0.2.0 to 0.1.x crosses the same boundary in the other direction.

Every standing seat rotates at its first wake after the deploy. The runtime-change rotation compares the running eve version and code fingerprint with the pair the seat last ran, finds them changed, and starts a fresh generation. The seat loses its working context, and its memory on disk stays. Each rotation writes one `session.runtime_rotation` audit row.

A conversation seat no longer runs a job inside its own turn. Each conversation seat (a domain seat, a thread seat and a DM seat) forwards the job with `work` to its own work session, which starts the worker with eve's `agent`. The seat holds `work` and `cancel_work` in place of `agent` and `task_cancel`, and the job's result wakes the seat later. A worker in a work session never waits on a person: it asks with `ask_room`, and an approval or a sign-in posts an OE card and returns at once. An app instruction that tells the seat to call `agent` or to wait for a worker no longer matches the seat's kit.

The `OE_AGENT_NAME` and `OE_AGENT_SHORT_NAME` env vars are retired, and nothing reads them. The agent's names now come from the `identity.name` and `identity.shortName` settings, and the slash command's name from `identity.commandName` (shipped `oe`). A deployment that set either env var and no setting answers to the brand names "open everywhere" and "oe" until you set the settings.

A declared subagent must not author `outputSchema`, because eve 0.67.0 removed it from `defineAgent` and it is now a typecheck error. A declared subagent must also author nothing at `tools/connection_search`, `tools/connection_execute` or `tools/connection_tools`: eve 0.69.0 and later RESERVE those slots, and `eve build` throws on any module there, a `disableTool()` sentinel or a no-op replacement included. Delete such files. A `disableTool()` sentinel at `tools/ask_question`, `tools/task_cancel` or `tools/todo` is a build error too ("disables a slot with no lower-precedence source"), because eve 0.69.0 and later no longer mount those tools. Delete it.

eve 0.69.0 and later refuse the file `agent/instrumentation.ts`: `eve build` exits 1 with "Found removed instrumentation file". Instrumentation is now the directory `agent/instrumentation/`, with one file per provider, and the file name is the provider slot. Every app scaffolded at 0.1.5 or earlier has the old file, so `oe upgrade` stops at its `npm run build` step until you move it (see the manual steps).

eve 0.71.0 owns the OpenTelemetry pipeline. On Vercel preview and production it registers its own tracer provider, for Vercel Agent Runs. An instrumentation file that also calls `registerOTel` stops every boot there with "another runtime already owns the global tracer provider", and every request fails with 500. The adapters instrumentation no longer calls `registerOTel`: its default export is eve's `otel()` declaration, with a trace policy that keeps model input and output out of every span, and the boot setup. The OTLP collector that `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` names is now an eve destination in a second slot file, `agent/instrumentation/otlp.ts`. An app that wrote its own exporter moves it into an `otelIntegration()` file (eve's instrumentation migration guide).

`eve build` prepares each sandbox template at build time on eve 0.69.0 and later. Off Vercel the backend is `docker` unless `OE_SANDBOX_BACKEND` names another one, so `npm run build` exits 1 when no Docker daemon is reachable ("The Docker sandbox provider requires a running Docker daemon"). That includes the `npm run build` step of `oe upgrade` on a machine whose app deploys to Vercel, because a local build is off Vercel. A build on Vercel prepares the Vercel Sandbox template instead.

The approval judge ships armed: `approvals.judgeMode` defaults to `enforce`, where 0.1.x shipped `off`. In `enforce` mode the judge runs a judge-deferred act (opening a pull request, creating a routine, sending an access request, and a connector write on the domain's credential) with no card ONLY when it cites one of the scope's authored pre-approval rules (`preApprovalRules` on a bundle), and the `approval.judge.verdict` row names that rule. An app with no authored rule keeps a card for every gated act, and makes no judge model call. An allow that cites no rule is now an ask, where 0.1.x `enforce` let an uncited allow run. Every admin act (`set_spend_limit` included) and every memory erasure (`purge_memory`) now always posts a card. An enforced cached allow is keyed on the act's arguments, the requester and attendance, where 0.1.x keyed it on the tool alone. A connector write (OPE-2368) reaches the judge only when it runs with the domain's credential in an attended turn that read no external content, in a room with exactly one domain, and an allow runs that one call only. A destructive connector op and an op on a person's own account keep their card. When the judge model cannot be reached or does not answer within 30 seconds, the card is posted. A consult costs up to two calls to the `judge` model role.

A click on an approval card in a conversation approves one act and keeps no grant (OPE-2363). A `pr.open` or connector-op card in a thread, a DM or at the top level of a channel offers Approve and Reject only, and a second identical proposal gets a card again. The "Approve for session" button is gone. Repeated approvals are the approval judge's job. Only a routine's `pr.open` card keeps its middle button, "Approve for this routine (up to N h)". That grant ends when it expires, when `revoke_session_grants` deletes it, or when an `edit_routine` moves the routine's key. Its clock is the renamed setting `approvals.routineGrantTtlHours` (shipped 24), which was `approvals.sessionTtlHours`; the config migration below moves an app's value. The boot refuses an app that still sets `approvals.sessionTtlHours`: `defineSettings` throws "unknown setting" at module load, and the overrides no longer typecheck. A grant that a 0.1.x click wrote is never read again. `revoke_session_grants` withdraws a routine's standing grants (pass `sessionId`), or every unspent one-call connector-op approval in a room (pass only `surfaceKey`).

configMigrations.description: Move the agent's names from env to `agent/settings/settings.ts`: the value of `OE_AGENT_NAME` goes to `identity.name`, and the value of `OE_AGENT_SHORT_NAME` goes to `identity.shortName`. Set `identity.commandName` only if the Slack or Discord app uses a slash command other than `/oe`.

Rename `approvals.sessionTtlHours` to `approvals.routineGrantTtlHours` in `agent/settings/settings.ts` if the app sets it, and keep the value. The setting now times only a routine's standing grant (OPE-2363). The boot refuses the old key: `defineSettings` throws "unknown setting" at module load, so an app that keeps it does not start.

manualSteps: Before the deploy, let the jobs that are running settle. A job still running on the 0.1.x deployment after the deploy keeps running there; remove the 0.1.x deployment to stop it. After the deploy, check the `session.runtime_rotation` audit rows: each standing seat writes one at its first wake. From 0.2.0, a deploy that changes code also rotates each conversation's work session at its next forward: the job goes to a new work session on the new code, and a `work.session_rotated` row (trigger `runtime-changed`) records it. The jobs that the old work session holds finish on the old deployment, and their results still reach the room (OPE-2377).

Read the `roster.lock.json` diff, then commit it. The 0.2.0 packages contribute new tools, among them `work`, `cancel_work` and `ask_room`. `oe upgrade` runs `npx oe build --accept`, which records a decision for each of them; after a manual install, run it yourself. `oe build`, which runs before the app's build, dev, start and typecheck, refuses a lock that has no decision for a contribution.

Copy the template's `agent/instrumentation/otel.ts` and `agent/instrumentation/otlp.ts` into the app, and delete `agent/instrumentation.ts` if the app has it. `eve build` refuses the old file. `npx oe upgrade --plan` lists each new file as missing. A core at 0.2.1 or earlier does not name the old file. A later core prints `DELETE agent/instrumentation.ts` while the app still has it. Without `otlp.ts` the app boots, but it exports no spans to an OTLP collector.

Start the Docker daemon before `oe upgrade` reaches `npm run build`, if the app builds off Vercel and its `sandbox.selfHostBackend` is `docker` (core ships `docker`; a template app from 0.4.0 on declares `justbash`, which needs no daemon). A core at 0.8.0 or later needs no daemon for its own build step when the app's `build` script ends in `eve build`: when `npm run build` fails and `docker version` does not answer, it builds again with `npm run build -- --skip-sandbox-prewarm` and says so in one line (OPE-2353). eve says that output may not be deployable, so do not start or deploy it. A Vercel deploy builds again on Vercel. An older core stops at `npm run build` on a host with no daemon. Then run `npx oe upgrade` again: the retry runs the `oe` the install put in place, so on a target at 0.8.0 or later it resumes and passes the build step. `OE_SANDBOX_BACKEND=justbash` helps only a target below 0.4.0, because 0.4.0 retired that variable (OPE-2411).

Sync these template files from the `@open-everywhere/create` template of the version you install, if the app was scaffolded at 0.1.5 or earlier: `agent/lib/register-adapters.ts`, `agent/sandbox/sandbox.ts`, `scripts/ops-mcp.ts`, `README.md` and `.claude/skills/upgrade-open-everywhere/SKILL.md`. No 0.2.0 template was published, and no template file changed between 0.2.0 and 0.2.1. The app owns its scaffolded files, so `oe upgrade` changes none of them. `npx oe upgrade --plan` lists every file that differs. The `scripts/ops-mcp.ts` edit matters most: without it, `surface_manifest` renders the Slack and Teams app manifests with the shipped default names, not the `identity.*` settings.
Merge by hand, if you want them, the template changes to the app's own config files: `agent/instructions.md` (a successful `reply` ends the turn) and the comment in `agent/spend/checkpoints.ts`.

Decide the approval judge's posture. To keep 0.1.x behaviour (a card for every gated act), set `approvals: { judgeMode: "off" }` in `agent/settings/settings.ts`. To auto-approve routine acts, copy the template's starter rules (`agent/access/pre-approval-rules.ts` in a fresh `npx @open-everywhere/create` app) into your app, bind them at org scope as the template's `approval-policy` bundle in `agent/access/bundles.ts` does, review each rule, and deploy. An app that ran 0.1.x with `judgeMode: "enforce"` and no authored rules now gets a card where the judge used to allow on its own judgement.

releases.summary: Boot refuses an unwired Postgres selection, `oe upgrade` reports template drift, `oe-eve-patch` restores pristine eve over an older OE patch, every NOTICE declares the eve modification core ships, the universal manual ships inside `@open-everywhere/core`, `oe build --check` also checks the overlays, `oe upgrade` runs codemods from the target release, the status route keeps a durable record of verified Slack events, the seat rotation counter counts a cached token once, and eve patch part 10 makes `eve build` faster.
breaking: A deployment whose store selection is Postgres now REFUSES TO BOOT when no Postgres client is registered for it. Before this release the same deployment booted and failed at its first audit write, while `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` both passed. The usual cause is an `agent/lib/register-adapters.ts` from the 0.1.2 or 0.1.3 template, which registers the Neon client only when `OE_MEMORY_PROVIDER` or `OE_OPERATIONAL_PROVIDER` reads `postgres`. The refusal is one sentence in the deployment log. Sync that file from the template (see the manual steps), or run `npx oe upgrade --plan --to 0.1.5` to list every file that differs. The embedded PGlite floor is not affected.

`npx oe build --check` now also runs the overlay check over the five machine-owned overlays at their default paths: `agent/access/grants.generated.ts`, `agent/access/credential-bindings.generated.ts`, `agent/webhooks/hooks.generated.ts`, `agent/memory/config/agents.generated.ts` and `agent/identity/groups.generated.ts`. The check reads each one strictly: after the header, the file must hold data only, in the exact layout the codemod emits. An overlay that holds anything else, or data in another layout, now turns `oe build --check` red, where 0.1.4 passed it. Edit only the data, then run `npx oe overlays normalize` to re-emit it. A header that an earlier release wrote still passes, because the check reads the header for its shape, not its bytes.
manualSteps: Run the recovery commands that `oe-eve-patch` prints, if it cannot fetch eve@0.54.3. This release adds part 10 to `patches/eve+0.54.3.patch` with the eve peer unchanged, so a tree that already ran `oe-eve-patch` keeps an eve that holds the 0.1.4 patch. The 0.1.5 `oe-eve-patch` restores pristine eve from `npm pack eve@0.54.3` and applies the patch again, in a checkout and on a build host that restores a cached `node_modules` alike. With no registry access and no npm cache, the `postinstall` exits 1, leaves eve unchanged and prints the commands: delete `node_modules/eve`, then install again.

Sync these template files from the 0.1.5 `@open-everywhere/create` template, if the app was scaffolded at 0.1.4 or earlier: `agent/lib/register-config.ts`, `agent/lib/register-adapters.ts`, `agent/sandbox/backend-select.ts`, `agent/sandbox/sandbox.ts`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md` and `.claude/skills/upgrade-open-everywhere/SKILL.md`, and add `agent/lib/register-docs.ts`. The app owns its scaffolded files, so `oe upgrade` changes none of them. The `register-docs.ts` and `register-config.ts` edits matter most: without `register-docs.ts` and its import in `register-config.ts`, `read_docs` serves the provider runbooks only, as on 0.1.4. With them, the manual follows the installed core version. The other changes in this window are comments and docs. A 0.1.5 core lists every file that differs in `npx oe upgrade --plan`.

Merge by hand, if you want them, the template changes to the app's own config files: `agent/instructions.md` (the hint that names the notion-rest skill's `page markdown current` command, on the line that ends "never put an id you inferred"), and comment-only changes in `agent/access/network-access.ts`, `agent/blob/hosting.ts` and `agent/spend/checkpoints.ts`. The five overlays (`*.generated.ts`) carry a newer header too: `npx oe overlays normalize` refreshes it, and the old header still passes the check.

Review `rotation.tokenBudget` and `rotation.contextSizeTokens` if you lowered either one to offset early seat rotation. Before this release, the counter added the cache-read tokens to `inputTokens`, which already holds them, so a cache-heavy seat rotated early. Each cached token now counts once, and the shipped thresholds are unchanged. With an unchanged override, a seat therefore rotates later than on 0.1.4.

releases.summary: Agent-led setup on two routes, Postgres by default on DATABASE_URL with a status route to read, Slack installed from `/setup`, and the scaffolder renamed to `@open-everywhere/create`.
breaking: The MEMORY backing is derived from `DATABASE_URL`. A deployment that holds a connection string and never set `OE_MEMORY_PROVIDER` was on the `git` floor before this release, and is on Postgres after it. Nothing errors: every unpinned tier reads an EMPTY Postgres store, and the agent reads as though it has forgotten what it learned. The git store is untouched, and simply no longer read. Choose a route before you deploy — see the manual steps.

The OPERATIONAL store is Postgres by default: hosted when `DATABASE_URL` is set, else the embedded PGlite floor. `sqlite` is deprecated, and reachable only by naming it in `OE_OPERATIONAL_PROVIDER`. A deployment that holds a connection string and never set `OE_OPERATIONAL_PROVIDER` was on the sqlite floor before this release and is on hosted Postgres after it. Nothing errors, and the audit chain, the spend ledger, the routine run-status and the break-glass connector revocations are all read from an EMPTY store — so a recorded `revoke_connector` stops being enforced, spend caps reset, and scheduled routines stop firing. The per-boot sqlite deprecation notice goes quiet at the same time, which removes the one signal that named the old state. The shipped `docker-compose.yml` pins the provider, so the shipped Docker route is unaffected; a self-rolled host is the exposed case.

The install wizard, the quickstart plan tool and the local goal are retired. Setup is agent-led now, on two routes: Vercel and Docker. The scaffolded app carries `AGENTS.md`, a `.mcp.json` that starts the `open-everywhere-ops` MCP server, and the `quickstart-open-everywhere` skill, so a coding agent drives the setup.
The scaffolder publishes as `@open-everywhere/create`. The unscoped `create-open-everywhere` name is retired rather than bumped: it keeps pointing at the releases up to and including 0.1.3.

`@open-everywhere/core` withdraws the retired wizard's public API. `agent/adapter-api.js` and `agent/adapter-api-ops.js` no longer export `registerQuickstartSurfaceGoal`, `PlanStep`, `SurfaceGoalStep` or `SurfaceHostedPlan`, and `agent/ops/quickstart.js` drops those four plus `quickstartPlan`, `Goal` and `PlanFacts`. A provider bundle that registered a setup plan through that call drops it: the step list `@open-everywhere/create --check` reports replaces it.

`StatusVersions.core` is `string`, no longer `string | null` (`@open-everywhere/core/agent/ops/status.js`). The status route always answers a real core version now, so a reader that branched on `core === null` must drop that branch, and a caller that injects a version bag into `deploymentStatus` must stop passing `core: null`. Both are compile errors on the upgrade, never a silent change.

`PreflightTarget` (`@open-everywhere/core/agent/ops/quickstart.js`) is now `"local" | "vercel" | "docker"`. The `"hosted"` member is gone. In TypeScript a caller passing `target: "hosted"` is a compile error. In JavaScript it is worse, because it matches neither deployment route: the gateway exemption and every route-specific sentence then answer as though the deployment were Docker, so a correct Vercel deploy can be reported not ready. Pass `"vercel"` or `"docker"`.

`@open-everywhere/core/agent/observability/telemetry.js` no longer exports `resetTelemetryConfigCache` or `resolveInstanceId`. Both existed for the retired install wizard's mid-process collector redirect. `__resetTelemetryForTest` is the remaining reset seam.

`GET /eve/v1/oe/status` is a NEW PUBLIC, UNAUTHENTICATED route on every deployment. It is built to be safe to publish — no secret, id, hostname, content or count — but it does disclose this deployment's contract posture (including `sandbox-backend` and `egress-control` verdicts) and its exact core version to any caller that knows the host. To hide it, exclude `channel/oe-status` in `roster.config.ts` or block the path at the edge. `docs/deploy/contract.md` § Hiding the status route gives both recipes, and `docs/deploy/surfaces/slack.md` § Public exposure covers a Vercel custom domain.

The Slack bundle mounts `GET`/`POST /setup` and `GET /setup/callback` on every deployment that registers it. The page is OPEN, and the deployment logs a one-time setup code on every start while it is, unless a Slack install is already recorded, `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` or `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET` is set in the environment, or `OE_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is unset or malformed. 🔴 A deployment that ships the Slack bundle but does NOT use Slack meets none of those conditions, so it upgrades into an open setup page. The trust root is read access to the deployment's logs — a platform permission (`vercel logs`, `docker logs`), not this product's `admin` role — so whoever holds it can complete the setup and bind a Slack app to this deployment. The lock fails closed and the page closes for good at the first install. Block both paths at the edge, or drop `slack-setup-page` from the roster, if the deployment will never use Slack.

configMigrations.description: `npm create @open-everywhere <dir>` (or `npx @open-everywhere/create <dir>`) replaces `npx create-open-everywhere <dir>`. An app scaffolded at 0.1.3 or earlier pins the retired name, so `oe upgrade` RENAMES that dependency instead of bumping it. An app below 0.1.4 reaches this release or a later one through the section "An app below 0.1.4" in UPGRADING.md.

`OE_MEMORY_PROVIDER` and `OE_OPERATIONAL_PROVIDER` are no longer needed on a hosted deploy. A present `DATABASE_URL` selects Postgres for both, and either variable still overrides that in either direction.

manualSteps: Choose the memory backing BEFORE you deploy this release, if the deployment already holds a `DATABASE_URL` and never set `OE_MEMORY_PROVIDER`. Set `OE_MEMORY_PROVIDER=git` to pin exactly today's behaviour, or migrate the memory first and let the derived default take effect. `docs/deploy/database-graduation.md` states both routes.

Choose the operational backing BEFORE you deploy this release, on the same test: the deployment holds a `DATABASE_URL` and never set `OE_OPERATIONAL_PROVIDER`. Set `OE_OPERATIONAL_PROVIDER=sqlite` to pin exactly today's behaviour, or bring the rows across first with `DATABASE_URL=… npx tsx scripts/migrate-operational.ts` from `packages/core` and let the derived default take effect. The migration copies the audit chain verbatim and verifies it at the target. `docs/deploy/database-graduation.md` states the route.

Re-apply the Slack app manifest, then REINSTALL the Slack app. This release subscribes the manifest to every event the front route reads, and adds the `mpim:history`, `files:read` and `files:write` scopes. Slack grants a new scope only on an install, so a manifest update alone leaves the app short.

Install Slack from the `/setup` PAGE if this deployment has no Slack credentials yet. The page asks first for the one-time setup code, which the deployment logs on every start while Slack is not installed — read it with `vercel logs` or `docker logs`. It then takes one pasted Slack app configuration token, and writes every credential Slack issues to the encrypted store. The page answers 404 while `OE_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is unset or malformed, or a Slack install is already recorded, and it closes entirely while `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` or `SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET` is set in the environment — an env-configured deployment keeps its credentials and skips this step. `docs/deploy/surfaces/slack.md` walks the page through.

Read `GET /eve/v1/oe/status` after the deploy to confirm the result. It answers one verdict per deployment-contract requirement id, and it reports the core version it is running. `docs/deploy/contract.md` explains the payload.

Sync these template files from the 0.1.4 `@open-everywhere/create` template, if the app was scaffolded at 0.1.3 or earlier: `agent/lib/register-adapters.ts`, `scripts/ops-mcp.ts`, `scripts/env-pipe.mjs`, `AGENTS.md`, `.env.example`, `README.md` and `.claude/skills/quickstart-open-everywhere/SKILL.md`, and add `.claude/skills/upgrade-open-everywhere/SKILL.md`. The app owns its scaffolded files, so `oe upgrade` changes none of them. 🔴 `agent/lib/register-adapters.ts` is the one that breaks a deployment: the 0.1.2 and 0.1.3 copies register the Neon client only when `OE_MEMORY_PROVIDER` or `OE_OPERATIONAL_PROVIDER` reads `postgres`. On this release a bare `DATABASE_URL` selects Postgres for both stores, so with the old copy a Vercel+Neon deployment registers no client and fails at its first audit write, while `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` both pass. A core that carries the boot refusal for this wiring names it in its own release entry. That core refuses to boot over the old copy instead, and its `npx oe upgrade --plan` lists every scaffolded file that differs from the target's template.

manualSteps: The ops deploy plan stops pushing AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, OE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL and OE_INTAKE_PAGE_SIGNING_KEY to the Vercel project. All three are still read where they are set, so remove one only to take the default: OIDC for the gateway, VERCEL_PROJECT_PRODUCTION_URL for the base URL, and a deployment-minted intake page key.
